home.headline: UCLA's defense leads the way in the rain for the 10-0 Bruins
home.blurb: It was another outstanding showing for UCLA defensive coordinator Colin Hitschler, as his team shut out Illinois in the first half and made it a homecoming to forget for Fighting Illini quarterback Katin Houser. Houser threw three picks and went just 16-34 through the air. Ty Dieffenbach went down but he wouldn't stay out in Week 11 Rain was always in the forecast for Saturday's game but the rain just kept falling in Pasadena. UCLA struck early and scored a first quarter touchdown before rain started to fall. From there, the game turned into a grinder, which is right up the Bruins alley. UCLA's defense starred yet again The scariest the UCLA defense looked all night was on the final drive of the game, just ask Houser. Houser left the game a few plays early after getting bloodied on a Sahir West sack. Scooter Jackson was a human seatbelt on Friday Scooter Jackson looked pretty scary in coverage too, grabbing two interceptions and having a prime chance at a third. Jackson is up to five picks on the year in a secondary of ballhawks. Derrick Barksdale grabbed an interception too. UCLA has forced the most turnovers in the country this season, averaging 3.0 takeaways per game. Aidan Mizell has another career game UCLA might have found lightning with Aidan Mizell. A week after scoring a pair of 75-yard touchdowns, Mizell snuck behind the Illinois defense for a 54-yard score. Mizell would have a 63-yard catch later in the game and wound up with 176 receiving yards. Who found Mizell on both of those throws? That would be Ty Dieffenbach. Dieffenbach had everyone in Westwood concerned late in the first half, going down with an injury after being hit on a dropback. Dieffenbach missed most of the third quarter but returned to lead UCLA on a touchdown drive, which would end up being all the Bruin defense would need. UCLA is partying like it's 1998, with the team enjoying its first 10-0 start in 28 years. With Bob Chesney at the helm, anything seems possible for No. 4 UCLA. picks.blurb: 2026 Week 11 Preview: Wake Forest Demon Deacons @ SMU Mustangs | Underdog Dynasty Skip to main content SB Nation SB Nation logo A Rest of the FBS Community Underdog Dynasty November 17, 2026 Underdog Dynasty Notifications Notifications The Feed Sections Conference USA Sun Belt Conference American Athletic Conference Betting FanDuel College Football Odds College Football Picks and Predictions Community Guidelines Login / Sign Up Search The Feed Sections Expand Conference USA Betting Expand FanDuel College Football Odds All communities Notifications ACC Wake Forest is rolling toward the ACC title game. But SMU, which has never lost a home ACC game, can stay in the race. Time and date: Saturday, November 14 at 12:00 p.m. ET Network: ESPN Location: Gerald J. Ford Stadium — Dallas, TX Spread: SMU (-1.5) Over/under: 61.5 All-time series: SMU leads, 3-1 Last meeting: Wake Forest 13, SMU 12 — October 25, 2025 Current streak: Wake Forest, 1 (2025) Setting the scene This might be the ACC regular season game of the year. For the first time in College Football Playoff history, the ACC champion is guaranteed an automatic bid. Thus, just getting access to Charlotte keeps the door ajar for Wake Forest and SMU in this high-stakes conference showdown. The Demon Deacons are one of the hottest teams in college football, winning six consecutive games, primarily in blowout fashion. But the Mustangs haven’t ever lost an matchup at Gerald J. Ford Stadium, faring 12-0 in their previous contests. A Wake Forest win propels the Demon Deacons to the doorstep of the ACC Championship Game. An SMU win creates chaos, bringing a cluster of 2-loss teams back into championship consideration, including itself. The ACC races greatly hinges on what unfolds Saturday afternoon on The Hilltop. Wake Forest Demon Deacons outlook Wake Forest (8-1, 5-1 ACC) is ranked No. 13 by the College Football Playoff committee, situated as the second-highest ACC team. Since its lone September loss to Miami (FL), the Demon Deacons have been as dominant as anyone in the FBS. During the last five games of its six-game win streak, Wake Forest has defeated opponents by an aggregate score of 264-31, or an average of 53-6 per game. The Demon Deacons used a dominant defense to stun SMU 13-12 in last year’s meeting in Winston-Salem, but this season, the offense has hit its stride under second-year coordinator Rob Ezell. Wake Forest ranks fourth nationally in scoring (43.3 points per game), ninth in total offense, and 10th in passing. Starting quarterback Gio Lopez missed last week’s game against FCS Merrimack with a lower body injury, but the absence was permissible due to the level of opponent. The former South Alabama and North Carolina gunslinger has been phenomenal in his new home, delivering 18 touchdowns against one interception this year, ranking 13th nationally in passing average. His mobility has made defenses pay too, accumulating 317 rushing yards and six touchdowns on the season. Lopez’s top target Carlos Hernandez is receiving national recognition. The senior is sixth in the FBS with an average of 105 receiving yards per game, and he regularly strikes from distance. Hernandez has multiple 70-yard touchdowns this season, and he has four outings with at least 110 yards and an end zone appearance. Jack Foley, Kam Shanks, and Antonio Meeks have provided support in this dynamic aerial attack, and the diversity in options allows Wake Forest to have the nation’s ninth-most efficient third down offense. The run game has been serviceable, ranking 43rd nationally in yards per game, while producing 4.94 yards per carry. Ty Clark and Deuce Lawrence have split carries throughout the season, totaling 416 and 327 rushing yards, respectively. Wake Forest’s offensive improvement has somewhat obscured the consistent impact of its defense. The Demon Deacons have only surrendered multiple scores once in their past five games, and they’ve finished 22 consecutive quarters without allowing more than seven points. The result is the country’s 13th-ranked scoring defense and 24th-ranked total defense — a unit which is particularly stingent against the run, surrendering just 85 yards per game on a 2.69 average. Defensive end Langston Hardy is the leader of the run-stuffing effort. He leads all ACC players with 13.5 tackles for loss, while also producing 44 tackles and 5.5 sacks. Backfield pressure has been a signature of this Wake Forest defense, and two other defensive linemen — Gabe Kirschke and Zach Lohavichan — have at least 7.5 tackles for loss. Wake Forest’s defense found the sustainable method of success, and that’s getting stops. The Demon Deacons are fifth nationally in both red zone defense and fourth down defense, finding ways to get off the field in critical situations. The unit can become even more dangerous if it dabbles in the turnover game. Wake Forest has forced just seven takeaways all season, which is tied for the eighth-fewest in the FBS. SMU Mustangs outlook SMU (7-2, 5-2 ACC) prepares for a revenge game against Wake Forest. Had the Mustangs prevailed last October in Winston-Salem, they would have competed in the ACC Championship Game with a College Football Playoff spot on the line. Instead, they fell in a 13-12 heartbreaker on a last-second field goal — one of the program’s four ACC losses since joining the conference in 2024. Zero of those losses transpired at Gerald J. Ford Stadium. SMU has been a different beast at home, and that was evident in its most complete game of the season last Friday against Virginia Tech. Counting games against FBS opponents, the Mustangs registered a season-high 23 first half points, utilizing its strongest start of the season to push past the Hokies, 51-28. The concept of senior day might have lost some luster in the transfer portal era, but Saturday will feature one of the most emotional senior day moments in recent memory. Kevin Jennings is in his fifth year with the program and third as the starting quarterback, and the Dallas area native has poured a lot into the program. Jennings guided the Mustangs to an American Conference title, an ACC Championship Game appearance, a College Football Playoff berth, and a Holiday Bowl victory. Now he’ll play his final game in Dallas, entering the pivotal matchup fifth nationally with 2,764 passing yards and fourth with 25 touchdown passes. The most remarkable part of Jennings’ eye-popping stats is his efficiency. For a quarterback that slings it deep quite often, the senior boasts a 73.9 completion rate, which is second among all players with at least 100 attempts. Jennings has also limited interceptions this year, finishing four of his last five starts without one. SMU’s high-powered passing attack involves a slew of receivers. Yamir Knight, coming off a 103-yard, 3-touchdown performance, is the most frequented with a team-high 50 catches. But Yannick Smith, Jalen Cooper, and Jalen Hale are also heavily involved — especially on downfield attempts — and all three average over 15.0 yards per reception this season. Tight ends Randy Pittman Jr. and Theo Melin Öhrström are also regular targets, tied for second on the team with four touchdown receptions apiece. The Mustangs’ run game is statistically a middle-of-the-road unit, ranked 70th in yards per game and 66th in rushing average. Kendrick Raphael operates as the top option, and he’s scored in seven of nine contests this year. Freshman Christian Rhodes has seen an increasing number of reps since mid-October, and he’s coming off a career-high 92 rushing yards against Virginia Tech. On defense, SMU displays a similar identity to the previous Mustang defenses of the Rhett Lashlee era: defensive line dominance. The Mustangs are one of 17 programs racking up at least 3.0 sacks per game, and defensive end Marques White is the ringleader of the movement. The eighth-year senior notched his third multi-sack game of the season last week, contributing to the turnover battle with a forced fumble and fumble recovery on the same play. But unlike the previous two seasons, SMU isn’t collecting turnovers on a consistent basis. The Mustangs have forced just eight turnovers all year, recovering five fumbles and picking off two passes. Despite the lack of takeaways, the secondary has shown considerable improvement from 2025, skyrocketing from 135th to 42nd in passing yards allowed per game, with safeties Jimmy Wyrick and Sael Reyes playing significant roles in that progress. Last year’s matchup between SMU and Wake Forest was the ultimate defensive battle. Just two touchdowns were scored — one on a 14-play drive and another capping a 41-yard series. There were eight combined turnovers in the matchup, which was decided on Connor Calvert’s 50-yard field goal as time expired. This year’s rematch looks bound to lean more on the higher-scoring end. Wake Forest brings significantly more offensive firepower in this matchup, headlined by the strong connection between Gio Lopez and Carlos Hernandez. The Demon Deacons’ offense has been virtually unstoppable since the start of October, and while SMU should provide some resistance with a formidable defensive line, Wake Forest will still get its points in Dallas. However, SMU can thrive in a shootout style game. The Mustangs are one of the most explosive offenses in the country, ranking ninth in the FBS with 15 plays spanning 40 yards. Wake Forest has excelled at preventing the big play this year, but the Mustangs’ receiving corps should present challenges on the back end that the Demon Deacons haven’t seen since the Miami (FL) loss. This back-and-forth thriller will come down to crunch time. With the backing of its home crowd, SMU improves to 13-0 in ACC matchups at Gerald J. Ford Stadium — a result which will add significant chaos to the final two weeks of ACC play. picks.headline: Wake Forest vs. SMU: Week 11 Betting Odds, Prediction
picks.blurb: Wake Forest enters the game with an 8-1 record, while SMU is 7-2. The game has significant implications for the ACC championship race. Betting odds slightly favor SMU, but the prediction favors Wake Forest in a high-scoring game. Week 11 of the College Football season gets us closer to the precipice of championship weekend. The ACC has a great slate to end the season, and Week 11 features a ton of awesome games. The showstopper is on at Noon ET, with the Wake Forest Demon Deacons taking on the SMU Mustangs. Wake Forest (8-1) has looked the part of a championship contender. There aren't a ton of takeaways from their 76-0 win against Merrimack out of the Football Championship Subdivision (FCS), but it continues a trend of dominance for them. The Demon Deacons. They haven't been within one score of a team since their upset win against Louisville earlier in the season, winning by 20+ in all of the past five matchups and 40+ in three of their past five matchups. SMU (7-2) should be closer to the ACC championship than they are. They proved it with a dominating 51-28 win against then 6-2 Virginia Tech, where their offense scored on nine of their 11 possessions. However, they dropped an easy game against Syracuse on Halloween. They lost 30-27, giving up a last-minute touchdown drive. That's been the only holdup preventing them from being in Wake Forest's spot. If you are looking for some betting advice for the matchup, we've got you covered. Here are the latest odds for the game, courtesy of BetMGM. Wake Forest vs. SMU game odds All college football odds via BetMGM Money Line: SMU -115, Wake Forest -105 Over/Under: Over 60.5 (-110), Under 60.5 (-110) Spread: SMU -1.5 (-105), Wake Forest +1.5 (-115) Wake Forest vs. SMU prediction, pick This might be the matchup with the most stakes in the ACC championship picture. If Wake Forest wins, they'll be 6-1 in the ACC and have tiebreakers over SMU and Louisville in the race, but if SMU wins, they'll be 6-2 in the ACC with one more game against Stanford remaining. If anyone's expecting the 13-12 defensive bout we got last year, throw that out the window. This should be a shootout. Both teams possess some of the best quarterbacks in the nation, with Gio Lopez and Kevin Jennings combining for 4,940 yards, 43 touchdowns, and seven interceptions. They're the biggest reason why either team is at the place it is now. Wake Forest has a few advantages, though. The Demon Deacons are one of the top teams in the nation at stopping the run, allowing just 82.9 yards per game (No. 5 in the country). The Mustangs are slightly above average against the run (133.9 yards per game, No. 45). The Demon Deacons are also favorites in the turnover battle. They're one of the most turnover-averse teams in the country (0.4 giveaways per game, No. 2 in the country), while the Mustangs are pretty turnover-prone (1.5 giveaways per game, No. 95). This game should have no problem hitting the over, with both of these teams boasting some of the top passing offenses in the league. However, give me the Demon Deacons in a road win. Safety Brauntae Johnson, who has been out since the season opening game against Wisconsin due to a foot injury, teased on his Instagram and shared by Pete Sampson on social media , that he could be returning this coming weekend against SMU. It would be a great sight to see, as he already deep secondary unit would become even better. This is turning out to be a very good timeline for his return, as he'll get a few games to get his feet wet before most likely playing in the College Football Playoff. Hopefully, Johnson is nearing a return, even if it isn't this weekend, as long as its before the regular season ends, it's a good sign for Notre Dame. picks.blurb: 3 Bold Predictions for Texas A&M Against No. 8 Tennessee in Operation Blackout Skip to main content SI.COM FOOTBALL FOOTBALL NEWS SI.COM AGGIES FB BASKETBALL NEWS SI.COM AGGIES BB The Texas A&M Aggies have their backs against the wall heading into Saturday's SEC showdown against the No. 8 Tennessee Volunteers. With bowl eligibility still in question, Mike Elko's squad will welcome one of the nation's top-ranked teams to Kyle Field for its annual Operation: Blackout game. Texas A&M enters the matchup looking to build momentum after an inconsistent season that has featured significant offensive struggles. Despite sitting at 4-5, the Aggies have shown flashes of defensive promise, allowing 20 points or fewer in five games this season. Meanwhile, Tennessee arrives in College Station following a dominant victory over Kentucky. The Volunteers have one of the nation's most dangerous pass defenses, leading the FBS with 39 sacks. However, with the home crowd behind them and plenty to play for, the Aggies have an opportunity to pull off an upset. Here are three bold predictions for Texas A&M against Tennessee. Texas A&M Holds DeSean Bishop Under 75 Rushing Yards Tennessee running back DeSean Bishop has been one of the Volunteers' most productive offensive weapons this season, averaging 118.4 rushing yards per game with 13 touchdowns. However, Texas A&M's defense will make stopping Bishop its top priority. With Tennessee losing backup running back Daune Morris for the remainder of the season, the Volunteers will likely depend even more heavily on Bishop. That could give Elko and defensive coordinator Jay Bateman an opportunity to load the box and force quarterback Joey Aguilar to win through the air. The Aggies have demonstrated the ability to keep opposing offenses under control, and Saturday could be another example. Prediction: Bishop finishes with fewer than 75 rushing yards and no touchdowns. 2. Marcel Reed Accounts for Three Touchdowns Without a Turnover Texas A&M quarterback Marcel Reed has struggled with consistency this season, particularly against ranked opponents. With eight interceptions, protecting the football will be critical against a Tennessee defense that thrives on creating pressure. However, Tennessee's biggest defensive weakness could provide Reed with an opportunity. The Volunteers have struggled against mobile quarterbacks, and Reed has the athleticism to exploit those problems. His performance against Arkansas, when he rushed for 66 yards and a touchdown on nine carries, showed what he can accomplish when the Aggies utilize his legs. Texas A&M Extends Its Operation Blackout Streak With an Upset Perhaps the boldest prediction is that Texas A&M pulls off the upset against the eighth-ranked Volunteers. The Aggies are 2-0 in Operation Blackout games under Elko, and Kyle Field could provide the extra energy needed to take down Tennessee. That's because Tennessee will win by a game-winning field goal, in my opinion. picks.blurb: Texas A&M Week 11 expert picks for matchup vs. Tennessee - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football College Football Playoff NFL Power Rankings Week 11 Waiver Wire Chargers get first win College football Top 25 Latest NFL updates Texas A&M Week 11 expert picks for matchup vs. Tennessee Jarrett Johnson, Aggies Wire · Aggies Wire Fri, November 13, 2026 at 10:00 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Texas A&M returns to Kyle Field Saturday afternoon, hosting No. 8 Tennessee in another difficult SEC matchup as the Aggies look to snap a four-game conference losing streak. Texas A&M enters the contest 4-5 overall and 1-5 in SEC play following a frustrating 17-9 loss to South Carolina. Despite finishing with 457 total yards against the Gamecocks, the Aggies struggled to finish drives, failing to score a touchdown despite several opportunities inside South Carolina territory. Tennessee enters Saturday's matchup 7-2 overall and 4-2 in conference play following an impressive 34-6 victory over Kentucky. The Volunteers have won two of their last three games, including victories over Alabama and Kentucky, but their recent struggles away from Knoxville could give Texas A&M an opportunity. The Aggies will need another strong defensive performance, particularly against Tennessee running back DeSean Bishop, who has surpassed 1,000 rushing yards this season. Offensively, quarterback Marcel Reed must find ways to sustain drives and avoid the mistakes that have plagued Texas A&M throughout conference play. Tennessee enters Saturday as a 2.5-point favorite , and most national experts are picking the Volunteers. However, at least one analyst believes Texas A&M can pull off the upset at home. Here is who the experts and prediction models are picking to win Saturday's matchup: Bill Connelly – ESPN SP+: Tennessee David Kenyon – Bleacher Report: Tennessee Pete Fiutak – College Football News: Tennessee Jake Margolick – College Football News: Texas A&M ESPN Analytics: Tennessee with a 58.6% win probability For Texas A&M, Saturday presents an opportunity to earn its first victory over a ranked opponent this season and take another step toward bowl eligibility. The Aggies must win two of their final three games to reach six victories, making the remaining schedule increasingly important. Tennessee leads the all-time series 3-2 and won the most recent meeting 20-13 in Knoxville in 2023. However, Texas A&M won the Volunteers' last trip to Kyle Field, securing a memorable 45-38 double-overtime victory in 2016. Saturday's matchup kicks off at 2 p.m. CT on ESPN. Despite having one of the Southeastern Conference's best home-field advantages, it won't be an easy task against one of the top-ranked defenses in the country in Tennessee . Entering the matchup with the Aggies, the Volunteers have 39 sacks, the most in all of college football and haven't allowed more than 27 points this season. On the flip side, quarterback Marcel Reed and his offense have scored at most 2 touchdowns against Power 4 opponents in the past month. To make matters worse, the Aggies became the first team in college football history to have over 450 yards, zero turnovers, and fail to score a touchdown in their latest loss to South Carolina. With those facts in mind, will the Maroon and White find a way to reverse their fortune, or will their matchup against the Volunteers be more of the same bland offense that has shown up for the better part of nine games? The two schools haven't met at Kyle Field in 10 years, when the Aggies won a wild double-overtime thriller, but let's see what the staff of Texas A&M Aggies on SI have to say about the outcome of this one. Tennessee 21, A&M 6 The last time the Aggies hosted a conference opponent at Kyle Field, they were victorious over the Arkansas Razorbacks, one of the lower-tier teams in the SEC. Marcel Reed has shown improvement in his play over the past two games, but Tennessee's defense is going to be his biggest test, and Tennessee running back DeSean Bishop will give A&M's run defense a run for their money as well. But A&M's run defense has shown their stinginess against prime running backs, and scoring in the red zone this year against A&M's defense is an impressive feat to pull off. If they can keep that rolling against the Vols, then SEC win number two is well within range for the Maroon and White, especially if George MacIntyre is starting. A&M could be P.O.ed just enough to make that happen. A&M 28, Tennessee 24 It's hard to have confidence in the Aggies offense, and it's even tougher to believe in them going against one of the best defenses in the country. The Volunteers should take advantage of a team playing uninspired football and handle business. Tennessee 31, A&M 10 Kolton Becker A&M needs this game to avoid having to win the next two games to become bowl-eligible. Does that mean it can happen? We'll find out more Saturday, but a lot of the numbers indicate that Tennessee's defense and offense should be able to take care of business. I think that happens. Tennessee 38, A&M 30 Two great defenses, one miserable offense. But a blind squirrel finds a nut once in a while. Maybe with a cold breeze, this will be the time. Tennessee (7-2, 4-2 SEC) is coming off a stellar second half against Kentucky, turning a tight game into a route in the fourth quarter and a 34-6 win on Nov. 7. The Aggies (4-5, 1-5) may be the most disappointing team in the SEC this year, but they have been competitive in recent road losses to Alabama and South Carolina. The Vols were ranked No. 8 in the latest CFP rankings , with Alabama surprisingly remaining well out of grasp at No. 3 despite Tennessee's win over the Tide last month. Here are Knox News' staff predictions for Tennessee-Texas A&M: Tennessee-Texas A&M expert predictions Adam Sparks, UT beat reporter: Tennessee 27, Texas A&M 17 The Vols need to win a road game after a big home win over a Top 10 opponent. That didn't work out a few weeks ago, but Texas A&M doesn't carry a UT curse like South Carolina does. This game will be decided inside the 20, where UT has the SEC's best red-zone offense and Texas A&M has the SEC's best red-zone defense. Look for George MacIntyre to hit some key passes to complement the ground game and dominant defense. Emmett Siegel, UT beat reporter: Tennessee 30, Texas A&M 20 This is another chance for Tennessee to stumble on the road after an emotional win like it did at South Carolina, but that Gamecocks team is much more dangerous than this one at Texas A&M. The formula is simple for the Vols: avoid penalties and turnovers and hand the ball off to Bishop. That should be enough to get the job done. Cora Hall, UT beat reporter: Tennessee 31, Texas A&M 14 The Vols will carry their momentum from a big win over Kentucky into a crucial win on the road. Regardless of who's at quarterback, no one has been able to slow DeSean Bishop down the last five games, and I don't see the Aggies being the ones to break that streak. Stephen Thompson, UT beat reporter: Tennessee 24, Texas A&M 13 This Tennessee defense has contained far better offenses and should have little trouble with Marcel Reed and Co. It will be another tight game until the Vols running game and DeSean Bishop deliver enough body blows to break through for explosive plays in the fourth quarter. Wynton Jackson, sports reporter: Tennessee 30, Texas A&M 15 The Vols have leaned fully into an identity of ball control football with a powerful run game and suffocating defense. It should carry them to another SEC win against an inconsistent Aggie offense that has struggled heavily in conference play. JOHN ADAMS: CFP's ranking of Alabama, Tennessee still doesn't make sense John Adams, columnist: Tennessee 24, Texas A&M 13 A dreadful Aggies season hasn't been devoid of entertainment, provided you have a sense of humor. In fact, I was chuckling at the Aggies' expense while wondering if Texas A&M receivers were wearing mittens against South Carolina. They dropped so many passes I expected quarterback Marcel Reed to feign an injury to his throwing hand and head for the locker room. However, Texas A&M receivers got upstaged by their defensive backs in the fourth quarter when injured South Carolina quarterback LaNorris Sellers outran the Aggies secondary despite a significant limp. Gentry Estes, Tennessean columnist: Tennessee 20, Texas A&M 10 To anyone who believes a school can just buy its way to a college football title these days, I'd present these Aggies as a rebuttal. In fact, Matthews left the medical tent on crutches and never returned from the locker room. ESPN and other outlets reported that his family was around him in the locker room and that he was unlikely to return to the sidelines. Luckily for Tennessee fans, Keys's talent level is through the roof, but we haven't had the opportunity to see that yet. Having Matthews out for the season isn't ideal, but there is a level of relief when you know the guy stepping in will be Keys. The first name worth noting is Travis Smith Jr. The talented receiver is a former four-star out of Westlake High School in Atlanta, Georgia, and is in his second season with the team. He showed some promise last season, but has shockingly had limited reps this season. He is a bigger body and will be best used on the outside due to the strength he produces. This means he will be key in setting blocks for DeSean Bishop, Javin Gordon, and the remainder of the running backs Tennessee has. Duarte is a transfer who was brought in to be a returner originally, and that is something he is likely going to do now that Daune Morris and Dodson are both out, and were key returners. Most of his work will be done in the kick return game, while Qua Moss is likely going to hold his punt returner spot, especially after a great showing against the Texas A&M Aggies on Saturday. The Tennessee Volunteers have officially lost one of their key receivers and players as a whole for the season. This leaves Tennessee with plenty of questions, including about depth. home.headline: Tennessee Volunteers Suffer Major Injury Blow vs. Texas A&M
home.blurb: George MacIntyre has been handling most of Tennessee’s quarterback snaps, with Brandon returning to a limited role after a shoulder injury earlier this season. Losing Matthews would remove the team’s top receiving option as the Vols try to improve their passing attack. Tennessee wide receiver Mike Matthews left Saturday’s game against Texas A&M on crutches after suffering an apparent right knee injury, dealing the Volunteers a concerning setback in the middle of a crucial SEC road game. Matthews, Tennessee’s leading receiver, was seen with a brace on his knee as he headed toward the locker room. The extent of the injury was not immediately known, but the scene raised concerns for a Vols team trying to stay in the College Football Playoff race. Mike Matthews Leaves Tennessee Game on Crutches On3’s Nick Kosko reported that Matthews appeared to injure his right knee during the second quarter against the Aggies. Matthews had caught two passes for 42 yards before leaving. Tennessee trailed Texas A&M 7-3 when the injury occurred, then added a field goal to make it 7-6 with 6:01 remaining in the half. The situation looked particularly troubling as Matthews made his way off the field. “Horrible development for Tennessee and Mike Matthews,” 247Sports’ Ben McKee wrote on X. “ESPN said it was a right knee injury. Now he’s headed to the locker room on crutches with a brace on his knee and a towel on his head.” ESPN College Football also posted video of Matthews leaving the field on crutches. Rocky Top Insider reported that his teammates were visibly upset following the injury. There was no immediate announcement from Tennessee about the specific injury or how long Matthews might be sidelined. The use of crutches and a brace alone does not establish a diagnosis. Mike Matthews Injury Threatens Tennessee’s Passing Game Matthews entered Saturday as the Volunteers’ most productive receiver, leading the team with 37 catches for 566 yards and four touchdowns through nine games. He was averaging 15.3 yards per reception and had also scored a rushing touchdown. His production is well ahead of Tennessee’s next-leading receiver, Braylon Staley, who came into the matchup with 36 receptions for 309 yards and two touchdowns. Matthews had been one of the few consistent downfield threats in an offense that has relied heavily on running back DeSean Bishop. The Vols entered the weekend with Bishop having rushed for 1,066 yards and 13 touchdowns. The junior receiver also led Tennessee with seven catches for 85 yards in its win over Alabama. He caught a 24-yard touchdown pass from Faizon Brandon in last week’s 34-6 victory against Kentucky. Matthews finished the 2025 season with 53 catches for 813 yards and four touchdowns. Before the Texas A&M game, he had 97 career receptions for 1,469 yards and 10 touchdowns. The Trojans have a legitimate chance to shake up the Big Ten race, give their College Football Playoff resume another major boost and send a strong message about the direction of their program. The Trojans are gearing up for a season-altering matchup against the No. 9 Indiana Hoosiers on the road in Bloomington. While USC already has a signature win over the Buckeyes under its belt, another victory against a top-10 opponent would completely change the conversation surrounding its postseason chances. With so much on the line for both programs, here are three bold predictions for USC's matchup with Indiana. 1. However, that number doesn't tell the whole story when it comes to the Hoosiers' ability to defend high-volume passing attacks. USC is averaging 294.5 passing yards per game while completing 67.3 percent of its attempts. USC quarterback Jayden Maiava has been a major reason for that success, throwing for 2,525 yards and 20 touchdowns while completing 67.3 percent of his passes. The Trojans also have no shortage of weapons for Maiava to work with. Freshman wide receiver Trent Mosley leads USC's receiving corps with 32 catches for 512 yards and six touchdowns, while fellow freshman Kayden Dixon-Wyatt has recorded 32 receptions for 443 yards and four touchdowns. Indiana's defensive numbers are certainly impressive, but the Hoosiers have shown some vulnerability against teams capable of consistently moving the football through the air. Those struggles could create a significant opportunity for a USC defense coming off its best performance of the season. Offensively, USC has the firepower to take advantage of the matchup. Indiana coach Curt Cignetti famously led his team to a national championship victory a season ago, but the Hoosiers' hopes of repeating a perfect season were dashed by No. 12 Ohio State. Indiana has looked vulnerable, though, needing overtime to win its last two games against Michigan and Minnesota. USC Trojans Coach Lincoln Riley on Indiana Hoosiers When previewing USC's matchup with Cignetti's Hoosiers on Trojans Live, Riley was full of praise for Indiana, and he highlighted the overall experience on the Indiana roster. "Really good football team. Definitely one of the more explosive offenses in the country. They return a lot of good players. They have multiple great wide receivers and an experienced quarterback. They're good at the running back position and offensive line," said Riley. "It's just a really good group, and there's a lot of continuity in that group and I would say a lot of the same things about them defensively. They have a really strong defense that returns a lot of guys from a year ago. It's a very deep talented front It's probably one of the deepest groups that we've played all year. picks.headline: Former Notre Dame head coach picks USC to beat Indiana
picks.blurb: Former Notre Dame head coach picks USC to beat Indiana - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football College Football Playoff NFL Power Rankings Week 11 Waiver Wire Chargers get first win College football Top 25 Latest NFL updates Former Notre Dame head coach picks USC to beat Indiana Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads As USC football prepares for a season-defining game at Indiana , one very interesting plot twist has emerged: A former Notre Dame head coach picked the Trojans to beat Curt Cignetti and the Hoosiers. Brian Kelly, now a commentator for CBS Sports, knows what it's like to coach in the state of Indiana. He recently said on air that Lincoln Riley's Trojans will go into Bloomington and win. This is not an earth-shaking story which possesses overwhelming significance, but it's a story worth noting because it's so fascinating on multiple levels. Brian Kelly had the upper hand over and against USC in most of the years he coached Notre Dame. Why is he trusting USC now? Notre Dame and Indiana fans had a very spirited argument before and after the Fighting Irish 's victory over the Hoosiers in the 2024 College Football Playoff. Notre Dame finished as the 2024 runner-up. 2025 Indiana, under Curt Cignetti, went one step beyond the Irish and won the national championship. Brian Kelly has no real reason to pick games for any reason other than he sincerely thinks one team will beat the other, but it's notable that he would trust USC and distrust Indiana. Both schools' fan bases don't like Notre Dame. It is simply interesting to wonder why Kelly is pivoting to the Trojans and away from the Hoosiers. Is there any underlying emotional reality which might have nudged Kelly in the direction of USC? Let's keep in mind that Kelly wants to return to coaching. Is his USC pick in any way motivated by how he sees the coaching carousel or the national landscape? We'll never know the answers, but the questions are legitimately interesting. It'll be the first meeting between the Hoosiers and Trojans since the latter program joined the Big Ten ahead of the 2024 season. It's especially important now given Indiana's recent tumble all the way down to No. 9 in the latest College Football Playoff rankings despite coming off of a bye. Josh Hoover has been, rather notably, dealing with an injury he suffered in the second half against Ohio State for several weeks now. At 5-4 and coming off an embarrassing 15-6 loss to Michigan State, Michigan desperately needs something positive. Unfortunately, that opportunity comes against No. 18 Oregon inside Autzen Stadium, one of the loudest and most intimidating venues in college football. The Ducks will have the benefit of a hostile home crowd, while Michigan will be breaking in a new offensive coordinator and attempting to find some semblance of consistency on that side of the ball. It's hardly an ideal combination. When Michigan Has The Ball All eyes will be on interim offensive coordinator Jim Harding , who takes over following Kyle Whittingham's decision to fire Jason Beck. Michigan enters the matchup ranked No. 126 nationally in scoring offense, No. 109 in rushing offense, No. 125 in passing offense and No. 132 in total offense. Those numbers are remarkably poor for a program with Michigan's resources and expectations. Whittingham hasn't officially named freshman Tommy Carr the starter, but all signs point to No. 14 manning the offense. Carr has shown flashes since replacing Bryce Underwood, but he's also operating behind an offensive line that has struggled throughout the season. Against Oregon, those protection issues could become even more glaring. The Wolverines need Jordan Marshall and Savion Hiter to establish something on the ground, particularly early. Otherwise, Carr could find himself facing obvious passing situations against an aggressive defense with the Autzen crowd making communication difficult. Harding doesn't need to reinvent the offense overnight. He needs to simplify things, establish manageable situations and give Carr opportunities to succeed. When Oregon Has The Ball Michigan's defense has been the more reliable unit by a mile, and that group will need another outstanding performance to keep this competitive. Defensive coordinator Jay Hill has enough talent to make things difficult, particularly with players like John Henry Daley, Zeke Berry, Chris Bracy and Jyaire Hill capable of creating disruptive plays. But Oregon presents a different challenge. The Ducks can put considerable pressure on a defense through tempo, athleticism, pure speed and offensive versatility. Michigan cannot afford repeated three-and-outs that force its defense to spend the afternoon on the field. If Oregon establishes an early lead, the Wolverines could find themselves in serious trouble. Michigan's defense should compete, but expecting Harding to completely transform one of America's worst offenses in less than a week is unrealistic. Autzen Stadium only makes matters worse. The Wolverines keep things respectable early before Oregon pulls away, leaving Michigan with two remaining opportunities to secure bowl eligibility. Oregon 27, Michigan 10

(Photo by Gregory Shamus/Getty Images) | Getty Images Von Lozon · SB Nation Fri, November 13, 2026 at 1:00 PM UTC · 9 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Michigan Wolverines travel all the way to the West Coast for a conference bout against the Oregon Ducks (3:30 p.m., FS1). In this week's Roundtable, Maize n Brew staff members give some takeaways from last week's game against MSU, some bold predictions for tomorrow's game and more! As always, let's reflect on last week's game. Provide any takeaways you had from the MSU game. Von : My takeaway is that this coaching staff should consider themselves lucky to still have jobs here. If it weren't for Warde Manuel resigning at the end of the year, as well as the university waiting for the president to begin her term next month, Kyle Whittingham may have been the one fired, not just Jason Beck. That game last weekend was as embarrassing a loss as I remember my time being on this planet, and that includes the dreaded 2020 season, App State, and everything to do with Rich Rod and Brady Hoke. It was truly that bad. Matt : It's over. Any shred of hope we had about the Whittingham era is now gone. To be incapable of scoring points on THAT Michigan State defense missing half its starters until garbage time is unacceptable. To then throw the players under the bus in the postgame press conference is an abomination. When futility stats that have existed for 90+ years are being broken, action has to be taken. Grace : Yikes! What a rough watch. It's disappointing and I feel for guys that have stuck with Michigan. Rod Moore, Zeke Berry and Jyaire Hill come to mind. While Kyle Whittingham doesn't seem to understand what this school is about, I think those guys do and this is just a terrible way for this season to continue. Scotty : My biggest takeaway is that we have officially hit rock bottom. What an embarrassing loss. Draw a line in the sand — do you want this coaching staff back next year? If you would keep some coaches but make changes, explain what you would do. Von : The only one I would entertain coming back is Jay Hill — he has been Harry Houdini in a season otherwise devoid of magic. So yes, I'd try and keep Hill around, but if the only way to guarantee Whittingham isn't back next year is if Hill can't come back, I'd be completely fine with it. I would do my best to hire away Bob Chesney from UCLA, knowing that is unlikely to happen. If he says no, open up the search even more and hope to God someone better is out there. Kellen : I'd keep Jay Hill, but everyone else can go. It took Whittingham too long to care to make a change like he did on Sunday. There's no sense of urgency. Matt : I would love to keep Jay Hill and some of the defensive staff. However, I want Whittingham and the entire offensive staff gone so badly that I would be willing to sacrifice the entire staff in order to start over. Even if the offense does get better under interim coordinator Jim Harding, Whittingham cannot be back under any circumstances or else the program will fall even further into disarray. Nick : Jay Hill and anyone he wants to keep from the defensive staff should be the only coaches that stick around next year. Kyle Whittingham clearly is asleep at the wheel and isn't the man for the job that we thought he would be when he was first hired. Despite all the drama and bad play that this season has brought, Hill and his side of the ball have been total pros about everything, and I think that's something you can't let get away. Whether it be making him the next head coach permanently or giving him all the money in the world to stick around with a new head coach, I think the school has to consider doing whatever it takes to keep him in town. Grace : No. I don't. I understand if it doesn't happen, but the way Whittingham is already talking about 2027 recruits and the transfer portal as solutions is just a way of saying "I'm not the problem, it's the players." With Ohio State left on the schedule and some of these guys nearing the end of the careers, I think that's a bad look. Scotty : I would love Jay Hill to stick around. I'm iffy on some others, but Kyle Whittingham cannot be this team's coach next year. Oregon…do we even care about the game at this point? Are we at the point of apathy, or are we still fully engaged hoping this team makes a bowl game? Von : I'm rooting for the players to succeed, but man, these next three weeks can't go by fast enough. Kellen : I'm excited to see if the men's basketball team can bounce back from the UConn loss. That's a high quality opponent and a good test for the Wolverines. That's two games in a row against elite opponents (the first being Houston) that we haven't seen them look great against elite opponents. As for the women's team, the UConn win is up there as the best win in program history. That team has a legit chance at a national title run, has at least four WNBA players, and there's a non-zero chance that we're getting a KBA statue outside of Crisler before 2060. Does that answer your questions? Matt : Hello darkness, my old friend. Apathy has arrived in its purest form. Who cares about a bowl game anymore? You could have said 10 years ago that making a bowl game was great because it allowed for an extra month of practice and a chance to see a team play one more time. This year, making a bowl game is futile because a majority of these players will be somewhere else next year anyways. I would be somewhat surprised if Michigan could even field a team for the bowl game given the amount of players that are sure to opt out and enter the portal the day after the Ohio State game. Nick : I don't think there's any way Michigan wins this week with Oregon seemingly finding itself again. This might not be the best Oregon team we've seen in recent years, but it is still capable of handling business, especially against a Michigan team that's totally lost right now. As for the rest of the year, I think UCLA is a lost cause as well. I won't rule out anything with the Ohio State game with the Buckeyes' season falling off a cliff. I did watch that 2024 game with my own two eyes, too. I even went back to watch the highlights a few times to verify that Michigan did win, so nothing would surprise me on that front. Regardless of how things pan out the rest of the way though, Michigan's 2026 season is over and the program needs to wipe the slate clean for 2027. Grace : Every week I'll be hoping for the improbable. I'm rooting for the players, but I'm not enthusiastic or optimistic. Scotty : This is a weird one for me. Obviously I can never root against Michigan, but I can't stand to see Whit come back for another year. The season is over, and missing a bowl feels like the best bet to make sure he's gone. I'll be cheering for Michigan as always, but I won't care or be upset when the game ends with a loss. Give us a bold prediction for tomorrow's game. Von : The game is scoreless after the first quarter, but the Ducks outscore the Wolverines by at least four touchdowns the rest of the game. Kellen : Michigan scores the first touchdown of the game and then doesn't score again. Matt : Michigan rushes for negative yardage on the game. Nick : I think Bryce Underwood plays a significant amount of snaps. Tommy Carr looked pretty rough throwing the ball against Michigan State and the Ducks could eat him alive, especially behind an offensive line that's in utter shambles. Carr will get the start at least, but I don't think it'll last very long. Grace : Michigan doesn't get thumped. Scotty : Michigan gets shutout. What's the final score and why? Von (4-5): Oregon 42, Michigan 10. This won't even be close. After Whittingham's comments about Oregon's NIL this week, Dan Lanning will be out for blood, PJ Fleck style. Kellen (5-4): Oregon wins, 26-7. Unlike Michigan, Dan Lanning actually made changes when things looked bad and the Ducks' season has turned around. On the bright side, maybe there will be another Netflix screening that Michigan can get invited to in the beautiful fall Oregon weather; at least we know that one film is being watched. Matt : (5-2): Oregon: A mediocre amount, Michigan: 0. Oregon figured some things out last week in its upset win over Ohio State, and Michigan has figured out nothing offensively. Can the Wolverines even score a point? Nick (3-4): I've got Oregon winning, 31-7. The Ducks shouldn't have any problem winning this game, especially at home. I think Michigan could perhaps find the end zone once with a new play caller, but nothing more inspiring than that. I think Jay Hill can keep the Ducks from making this a true bloodbath at least. Grace (5-4): 24-21, Michigan. The defense makes huge plays on the road. The offense finds one tiny spark and Jason Beck isn't there to stomp on it, so we win. Scotty (2-4): 17-0, Oregon. Beck being fired was good to see, but it's not going to make a difference this season. The offensive line is horrendous, and now we have the offensive line coach running the offense. Great! The defense will be solid, but the offense will be painful.

picks.blurb: Oregon Predicted to Easily Handle Michigan This Week - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football College Football Playoff NFL Power Rankings Week 11 Waiver Wire Chargers get first win College football Top 25 Latest NFL updates Oregon Predicted to Easily Handle Michigan This Week (Adam Cairns/Columbus Dispatch / USA TODA) Matt Levine · Roundtable Sports Thu, November 12, 2026 at 12:02 AM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Oregon Ducks are in a good spot as the team enters the upcoming week of the college football season. Despite the Ducks having three losses on their resume, Oregon remains very much alive in the hunt for the College Football Playoff. In the new rankings for the playoff , Oregon came in ranked at No. 16, giving this team a real chance to get in. After taking down the Ohio State Buckeyes a week ago on the road, Oregon has put itself in a strong position to make some history. No team in the history of the playoff has reached the bracket with three losses, but this could be the year for it to happen. However, the Ducks will still need to win out for this to become any form of reality, and the team has three games left. First up for Oregon is a matchup at home against the Michigan Wolverines this weekend, with the Ducks feeling very confident heading into the game. With how the teams have played of late, Oregon is seen as the favorite to take down Michigan, giving this group more of a chance for the playoff. But the Ducks can't overlook the Wolverines, especially with their margin of error being so slim for the rest of the way. Bleacher Report's David Kenyon predicted the games of the week, including this matchup between Oregon and Michigan. In the prediction, Kenyon has the Ducks taking care of business against the Wolverines by a score of 28-13. Oregon starting quarterback Dante Moore is out for the rest of the year due to injury, and it's the Dylan Raiola show now. Raiola has given the Ducks some hope this season, providing a spark on offense. Raiola has thrown for 1,354 yards with 11 touchdowns and two interceptions in seven games played for the Ducks this year. Losing Moore hurt this team, but Raiola has brought a sense of calm to the entire offense, giving them a chance to make some history. Against Michigan, Raiola will be called upon again, with him needing to put together a strong showing. The Wolverines can be a tricky team, with freshman quarterback Tommy Carr expected to get the start again this week. Carr has shown some ability to handle college defenses, but the Ducks can't take him lightly. If Oregon can take down Michigan, it would bring them that much closer to a playoff appearance.

away.blurb: U-M (5-4, 2-4 Big Ten) will be without offensive tackle Blake Frazier in the Week 11 contest against Oregon (6-3, 4-2 Big Ten). He left last week's loss to MSU in the second half and was officially ruled out in the pregame availability report provided to the Big Ten two hours before kickoff (3:30 p.m., FS1). The Wolverines could also be without right guard Brady Norton, who got banged up a week ago as well and played just 26 snaps. Norton, who's listed as a game-time decision, missed Michigan's Week 7 win over Penn State but has been a consistent part of the rotation, playing 446 snaps (the fourth most of any offensive lineman on the team) this year. Tight ends Hogan Hansen and Jalen Hoffman, who were listed as questionable all week, were both removed from the report. Hansen missed the first two games of the season and then was banged up last week, playing just six snaps. Hoffman hasn't missed any time yet this season. U-M got good news on the defensive side of the ball. Edge rushers John Henry Daley and Dom Nichols and safety Rod Moore were all listed as questionable but have been removed from the report, indicating all are good to go. The only player missing (who hasn't been out the whole year) on the defensive side of the ball is edge Nate Marshall, who was suspended indefinitely earlier this week. The junior wideout only has two grabs for 32 yards this season but is frequently on the field, having played the third-most snaps (127) of any wideout, though Salesi Moa and Travis Johnson has been earning more playing time of late. home.headline: Michigan football vs Oregon game day injuries: OT Blake Frazier is out
home.blurb: U-M (5-4, 2-4 Big Ten) will be without offensive tackle Blake Frazier in the Week 11 contest against Oregon (6-3, 4-2 Big Ten). He left last week's loss to MSU in the second half and was officially ruled out in the pregame availability report provided to the Big Ten two hours before kickoff (3:30 p.m., FS1). The Wolverines could also be without right guard Brady Norton, who got banged up a week ago as well and played just 26 snaps. Norton, who's listed as a game-time decision, missed Michigan's Week 7 win over Penn State but has been a consistent part of the rotation, playing 446 snaps (the fourth most of any offensive lineman on the team) this year. Tight ends Hogan Hansen and Jalen Hoffman, who were listed as questionable all week, were both removed from the report. Hansen missed the first two games of the season and then was banged up last week, playing just six snaps. Hoffman hasn't missed any time yet this season. U-M got good news on the defensive side of the ball. Edge rushers John Henry Daley and Dom Nichols and safety Rod Moore were all listed as questionable but have been removed from the report, indicating all are good to go. The only player missing (who hasn't been out the whole year) on the defensive side of the ball is edge Nate Marshall, who was suspended indefinitely earlier this week. home.headline: Oregon Ducks lose top running back for second straight week
home.blurb: Jordon Davison (leg) was listed as out on Wednesday’s availability report ahead of the No. 16 Ducks’ matchup with Michigan. But it’s not all bad news on offense: freshman wide receiver Messiah Hampton, who missed several games amid legal issues , is not listed on the report. Presumably that means he will be available on Saturday, though Dan Lanning hasn’t spoken on Hampton’s status for the remainder of the season. After a season-ending injury to star edge rusher Teitum Tuioti, the Ducks also saw his replacement — Nasir Wyatt — added to the report as probable with an undisclosed injury. Some key defensive players have a designation for Michigan as well: safety Rod Moore and star edge rusher John Henry Daley are both questionable. Oregon football will be without its top running back for the second consecutive week. picks.headline: Ole Miss vs. Oklahoma Predictions: Why our Staff is Split on the Winner
picks.blurb: Ole Miss vs. Oklahoma Predictions: Why our Staff is Split on the Winner Skip to main content SI.COM FOOTBALL FOOTBALL NEWS BASKETBALL NEWS Ole Miss (6-3, 4-3) is back on the road this weekend, where it will meet the Oklahoma Sooners (5-4, 3-3) in Norman for a game that each side could really use in the win column. For Oklahoma, it won’t mean much in terms of a playoff push, but it will go a long way in salvaging what’s been a lost season. The Sooners don’t have consecutive wins (or losses) on the season yet, but they have collected wins over Texas and Florida in the last five weeks. For Ole Miss, its CFP hopes are on thin ice and to even be somewhat involved in the conversation next month, the Rebels badly need to win their final three regular season games. Ole Miss initially opened as a 2.5-point road favorite last week, but will now enter the weekend as a narrow 1.5-point underdog. Ahead of the Rebels' latest conference matchup, Ole Miss On SI predicts which team wins and why. Ole Miss On SI Staff Predictions Oklahoma Sooners quarterback John Mateer (10) runs beside Ole Miss Rebels linebacker Suntarine Perkins (4) during a college football game between the University of Oklahoma Sooners (OU) and the Ole Miss Rebels at Gaylord Family Ð Oklahoma Memorial Stadium in Norman, Okla., Saturday, Oct. 25, 2025. Ole Miss won 34-26. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect Tyler Komis This weekend will mark another notable challenge for Ole Miss on the offensive side of the ball. It’s not an ideal weekend to not have Patrick Kutas available either, arguably Ole Miss’ top offensive lineman over the past two seasons. Oklahoma brings a defensive front that’s up to nearly 30 sacks on the year and one of the best run defenses in the conference, entering game day. Ole Miss desperately needs to bounce back in both departments, as it surrendered five sacks and ran for just 66 rushing yards in its loss last week. While there’s no doubt Ole Miss’ offensive line will get tested, and that Oklahoma will be sending consistent pressure, I’m picking Trinidad Chambliss to capitalize on what is looking like his final test against a great collegiate defense. Though Ole Miss will be without its leading tackler in Keaton Thomas, Oklahoma’s offense shouldn’t pose much of a threat anyway. It’s a golden opportunity for the Rebels to get right on that side of the ball. I expect a close game in Norman, thanks to the Sooners’ defense, but if one team was going to separate itself by multiple scores I think it would likely be Oklahoma. Ole Miss 27, Oklahoma 20 Matt Galatzan Ole Miss needs to get back on track if it is going to save its season. Fortunately, Oklahoma is the perfect opponent to do just that. The Sooners have struggled mightily this season, and the Rebels have the best quarterback in the country, and their backs against the wall. I think Ole Miss wins, and wins big. Billy Flowers I can see this matchup going one of two ways: Ole Miss comes out of the week angry and inspired and beats the brakes off Oklahoma, or Oklahoma coach Brent Venables exploits the weaknesses the Rebels showed against Georgia, and the game is close. Unfortunately, I see the latter as more likely. I think Ole Miss' offense comes out flat, and the grocery list of injuries bites the Rebels in the back. I don't think the Rebel defense is strong enough to shut down Oklahoma's offense completely. I expect Oklahoma to weasel out a tight one. Oklahoma 23, Ole Miss 20 Coming off such an embarrassing loss to Georgia, I think Ole Miss bounces back this weekend against Oklahoma. I don’t think either team’s offense will be particularly strong on Saturday. However, I have more faith in Ole Miss’ offense to recover from a string of poor performances, even if Ole Miss linebacker Keaton Thomas is out and Jason Witten has taken over as the Sooners’ interim offensive coordinator and play-caller. Give me the Rebels by three points in a game defined by the two teams’ defenses. Ole Miss 27, Oklahoma 24 Cooper Ferguson Ole Miss is in desperate need of a bounce-back performance after getting embarrassed by Georgia last weekend. The Rebels have plenty of questions to answer offensively, especially with Kewan Lacy and Patrick Kutas out. Oklahoma’s defense is one of the toughest units in the SEC, and I expect Brent Venables to make life difficult for Trinidad Chambliss throughout the afternoon. However, I still have faith in Pete Golding’s defense to get the job done against an Oklahoma offense that is still trying to find its identity under Jason Witten. The Sooners looked better against Florida, but I need to see more before buying into the offensive turnaround. Ole Miss has too much at stake to let another opportunity slip away, and I expect Chambliss to lead a late scoring drive to secure a critical road victory. Ole Miss 24, Oklahoma 20 For Ole Miss, it comes down to scoring on the Sooners. Oklahoma lacks a sufficient run game, and at times, John Mateer can really struggle. If the Rebels lose, it will likely be because of that deadly defense. I predict that the Sooners defend their home territory and win 21-17 with a great defensive performance. I hope the Rebels prove me wrong, but they need to improve a lot, including their run game and tackling. The defense looks better, but the offense doesn’t do quite enough to defeat Oklahoma. picks.headline: Three Bold Predictions for Ole Miss' Trip to Oklahoma
picks.source: Ole Miss Rebels On SI on MSN
picks.blurb: No team should be judged by how they perform when everything is going its way, just as this Ole Miss program should be judged on how it can respond after the tumult it faced last time out against Georgia. With the Rebels' playoff hopes dwindling to the lowest they have been all season, Pete Golding's squad will need to respond in a big way this afternoon in Norman . Facing an Oklahoma team with a retooled offensive scheme and rejuvenated belief in itself, Ole Miss will need to capitalize on the trend that the Sooners have yet to win consecutive games this season. Just about everything went wrong at Vaught-Hemingway Stadium last weekend for the Rebels, and it's true; everyone has a plan until they get punched in the face. Golding's side took a clean hit to the jaw from the Bulldogs, and Ole Miss will need to claw itself up against Oklahoma if it wants a chance at getting back to the playoffs this season. Trinidad Chambliss Plays a Clean Game Following His Worst Showing Numbers talk, and for Trinidad Chambliss, they're quite damning. Throwing nine passes to the wrong side this season, the Rebels' former Heisman frontrunner is third in the Football Bowl Subdivision for interceptions this year. If Ole Miss wants to win on the road tomorrow and show that it can play in tough road environments, Chambliss will need to clean the turnovers up. The differences between Georgia and Oklahoma are clear, and I truly believe that Chambliss will return to the form he got fans used to in the 2025 season. The Rebels need their star to play a professional game today, and that all starts with taking care of the ball and making the right decisions when the Sooner pass rush gets in his way. The days of Chambliss and Kewan Lacy backfields are over this year, and the former will need to remind the Rebels' faithful of the leader he is capable of being. Behind a reworked offensive line, I expect Chambliss to erase the doubts that have been growing surrounding him recently, and #6 will lead Ole Miss to victory in Norman on the heels of a strong offensive showing. Shekai Mills-Knight has the Best Rushing Performance of the Season While Lacy's legacy in Oxford looks like it will end full of questions about injuries and unfulfilled potential, the Rebels have a tailback capable of reshaping the team's rushing narrative late in the season. I wholeheartedly believe in Ole Miss' French-Canadian sophomore, and John David Baker's offensive scheming needs to rely on the talent that can line up beside Chambliss. Shekai Mills-Knight, when utilized by Baker, has been a revelation for Ole Miss' rushing attack; the only issue is that Knight has been used nowhere near enough. Makhi Frazier has left a lot to be desired since arriving at Ole Miss from Michigan State, and with Knight receiving the leftover touches, the Rebels have seen what the sophomore back is capable of. If Shekai Mills-Knight is given an uptick in touches in Norman, there is no reason that the tailback cannot eclipse Ole Miss' single-game leading rusher this season: Kewan Lacy's 122-yard showing against Missouri. The Rebels need to be more dynamic offensively, and it all starts with feeding the Canadian native. The Defense Holds Oklahoma Under 21 Georgia's offense was able to do whatever it wanted in Oxford last weekend, and the Rebels will need to suffocate John Mateer and the Sooners under the new Jason Witten-led offense. Ole Miss has lived off of its offense for the past two seasons, and with how things have gone recently, a strong defensive showing in Norman will go a long way, not just towards a win but towards proving to the selection committee that the Rebels are worthy of making the postseason. Golding's defense has the talent to be great, now it just needs to translate to the field. Best Ole Miss vs Oklahoma props toda Prop pick #1: John Mateer Over 229.5 passing yards With Jason Witten taking over play-calling duties for the Oklahoma Sooners , John Mateer appears to be in great hands after a spectacular performance against the Gators a week ago. The Sooners' defense has held opponents to just 122.7 rushing yards per game this season . Meanwhile, Ole Miss is running the ball on just 45% of its plays, averaging 33.3 attempts per game. Between the injury uncertainty, inconsistent workload, and difficult matchup, I'm backing Frazier to finish below this number. There's no better quarterback to back than one of the nation's most dynamic playmakers, Ole Miss star Trinidad Chambliss . With Brent Venables' aggressive, blitz-heavy defense likely to pressure Chambliss, I expect the Ole Miss quarterback to have opportunities to leave the pocket and find open grass. 5 Ole Miss vs Oklahoma predictions with Trinidad Chambliss, Rebels' CFP chances on line
picks.blurb: 5 Ole Miss vs Oklahoma predictions with Trinidad Chambliss, Rebels' CFP chances on line - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football College Football Playoff NFL Power Rankings Week 11 Waiver Wire Chargers get first win College football Top 25 Latest NFL updates Sam Hutchens, Mississippi Clarion Ledger · The Clarion Ledger Thu, November 12, 2026 at 11:03 AM UTC · 4 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads OXFORD − Ole Miss football must win on the road against Oklahoma to keep hopes of a College Football Playoff appearance alive. No. 17 Ole Miss (6-3, 4-3 SEC) will play at Oklahoma (5-4, 3-3) on Nov. 14 (3:15 p.m., SEC Network). The Rebels are coming off a 42-7 home loss to No. 1 Georgia that put its CFP hopes on the edge of extinction. A viable path to the CFP begins with winning the final three games of the season. This is the third consecutive season Ole Miss has faced Oklahoma and the Rebels have won the first two matchups. Like Ole Miss, the Sooners made the College Football Playoff in 2025. OU returned quarterback John Mateer but has struggled to complement a strong defense with a steady offense. Although the Sooners have losses to Michigan, No. 1 Georgia, No. 13 Kentucky and No. 24 South Carolina, OU has beaten two teams that Ole Miss lost to in No. 8 Texas and Florida. Here are five predictions about the matchup, including the final score: Jason Witten will have new wrinkles for OU offense vs Ole Miss defense The matchup pits defensive coaches against each other in Ole Miss' Pete Golding and OU's Brent Venables. Interim offensive coordinator Jason Witten could be the wild card. The former Dallas Cowboys tight end was elevated to the interim offensive coordinator position after Oklahoma fired Ben Arbuckle. Five days after Arbuckle was dismissed, OU beat Florida 23-7 in a game where it had 351 total yards. The Oklahoma offense played clean, efficient football under Witten. The Sooners suddenly seem to have new life offensively, which comes at a bad time for an Ole Miss defense that was ravaged for 481 yards vs Georgia. Trinidad Chambliss, John Mateer both throw interceptions With three games remaining, Chambliss' interceptions have tripled this season. He threw three in a spectacular 2025 season, but is up to nine in 2026. Golding attributed the increase to a combination of bad reads, bad luck and bad throws. Chambliss has thrown at least one interception in seven games this season. That plays into the hands of Oklahoma, which is No. 4 in the SEC with nine interceptions. The Sooners are also No. 5 in the conference with 26 sacks. Chambliss has been more vulnerable when under pressure. OU quarterback John Mateer has had turnover problems as well. He's thrown seven interceptions and has two lost fumbles. Look for both defenses to come up with an interception. The Sooners' stingy defense is better prepared to recover from interceptions than Ole Miss. When OU picks off Chambliss, it will give the ball back to a Sooners' offense that looks well prepared to chew clock and limit the chances for the Rebels' offense. Ole Miss gives Makhi Frazier, Shekai Mills-Knight both at least 10 carries Even with a quarterback as capable as Chambliss, it will be hard for Ole Miss to attack Oklahoma through the air. OU has the No. 1 passing defense in the SEC (170.7 yards per game). OU is No. 7 in the SEC in rushing defense (122.6 yards per game), but it's the weaker of two stout options. Ole Miss needs running backs Shekai Mills-Knight and Makhi Frazier to play well. Those two players are the primary backs with Kewan Lacy ruled out with a shoulder injury. Mills-Knight and Frazier combined for 17 carries for 60 yards vs Georgia, but they should get more carries against Oklahoma. Oklahoma leads in time of possession, Ole Miss relies on big plays Opponents are 31-for-112 (27.7%) on third down conversions against the Sooners. That's the lowest mark in the SEC and No. 4 nationally. That indicates Ole Miss will have trouble maintaining long, slow-developing drives. The key to combat that is explosive plays. Ole Miss could use a big game from Deuce Alexander. The receiver leads Ole Miss with 669 receiving yards, but he was held without a catch against Georgia. He is Ole Miss' fastest, most explosive player and the primary threat to score a deep touchdown. Ole Miss is on the other end of the spectrum. The Rebels allow 44% of third down conversions, which is No. 14 in the SEC. The Sooners clinched the game against Florida with a 20-play march in the fourth quarter that consumed 12:45 on the clock. The Rebels must avoid that fate. Ole Miss vs Oklahoma score prediction Oklahoma 24, Ole Miss 23: This should be a close game that will be determined by whether Ole Miss' defense or Oklahoma's offense does better. Right now it feels like the OU offense has more momentum. The Rebels are more desperate, but feeling like you need to press and make big plays on the road against OU's defense is a bad place to be. picks.blurb: Sooners Wire Staff predictions for Oklahoma vs. Ole Miss - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football College Football Playoff NFL Power Rankings Week 11 Waiver Wire Chargers get first win College football Top 25 Latest NFL updates Sooners Wire Staff predictions for Oklahoma vs. Ole Miss Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Oklahoma Sooners (5-4, 3-3 SEC) and the Ole Miss Rebels (6-3, 4-3 SEC ) meet for the third straight season and the second consecutive season in Norman. Oklahoma is 0-3 all-time in the series but is coming off of one of its most complete games of the season in their win over the Florida Gators . The offense found a rhythm and consistency we haven't seen much this year, and the defense suffocated the Florida Gators, holding them to seven points and forcing two interceptions. This week, with the Rebels coming to town, the Sooners face a much different challenge. Ole Miss boasts one of the most dynamic quarterbacks in college football, in Trinidad Chambliss. Chambliss is 15th in the nation in passing yards and second in the SEC behind LSU's Sam Leavitt. He's a threat to make plays with his legs as well, as we saw last year in the Rebels' win in Norman. On a slippery Owen Field, Chambliss threw for 315 yards and ran for 53 yards in Ole Miss's 34-26 win over Oklahoma. The Sooners defense will need to do a better job containing Chambliss if they want to win this Saturday and earn bowl eligibility. Can Oklahoma find a way to earn back-to-back victories for the first time since the LSU and Missouri wins at the end of last season? Here's how our staff at Sooners Wire sees the game playing out. Sooners Defense Leads to Win Oct 10, 2026; Dallas, Texas, USA; Oklahoma Sooners defensive back Peyton Bowen (22) runs to score a touchdown against the Texas Longhorns during the second half at Cotton Bowl. Mandatory Credit: Kevin Jairaj-Imagn Images It'll be a battle between two defense-minded coaches, and the Sooners are still riding high with Interim offensive coordinator Jason Witten at the helm, while Ole Miss' offense is sputtering thanks to key injuries to its offensive line, star running back, and possibly the quarterback. For one of the few times this season, the injury report looks to be in favor of Oklahoma, which is looking to build on a win for the first time this season. With everyone theoretically healthy, one of the advantages Oklahoma has is that Ole Miss QB Trinidad Chambliss has become turnover-prone, throwing nine interceptions this season, while OU's defense does well at forcing those turnovers, coming in at No. 4 in the conference. It's no secret that the Sooners are typically successful when they win the turnover battle, and I think that will play a role in this one. It'll be a defensive battle, but OU will have the edge at home. Oklahoma 17, Ole Miss 14 James D. Jackson, Contributor Ole Miss Responds This season, Oklahoma has typically followed up an encouraging step forward with a discouraging step back, ever since the Texas game. Ole Miss is reeling after last week's loss to Georgia, and Brent Venables typically doesn't have his team as on point when the opponent is more desperate and hungry than the Sooners are. Things will probably slip after last week's upset win; there's too much of a pattern to think otherwise. If Trinidad Chambliss plays like he's capable of, Ole Miss wins. If OU recaptures some of the magic of last November, when the Sooners played consistent football, they can put an end to Ole Miss' teetering playoff hopes. Ole Miss 20, Oklahoma 17 Aaron Gelvin, Contributor Ole Miss has the Better QB Oct 31, 2026; Oxford, Mississippi, USA; Mississippi Rebels quarterback Trinidad Chambliss (6) drops back to pass during the fourth quarter against the Auburn Tigers at Vaught-Hemingway Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Petre Thomas-Imagn Images The Oklahoma Sooners continued their uneven play this season with a win over the Florida Gators. The Sooners have yet to win or lose back-to-back games this season. While it looked much better offensively under Jason Witten, the question is whether that will continue against the Ole Miss Rebels. This game is a true toss-up, but I've got to go with the quarterback I trust more and that's Trinidad Chambliss. Ole Miss 24, Oklahoma 17 Jaron Spor, Contributor Offense Does it Again Nov 7, 2026; Gainesville, Florida, USA; Oklahoma Sooners quarterback John Mateer (10) throws the ball during the first half against the Florida Gators at Ben Hill Griffin Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Matt Pendleton-Imagn Images The Oklahoma offense took a positive step in the right direction last week with their road win over Florida. They found a way to win with a ball-control style that helped the Sooners win the time-of-possession battle by 15 minutes. The Sooners scored on three of their first four drives, laying the groundwork for what could be the plan to keep Trinidad Chambliss and the Rebels' offense at bay this weekend. Ole Miss allows 394.7 yards per game, which is 15th in the SEC and 104th in the nation. This could be another opportunity for the Sooners' offense to take a big step forward. away.blurb: No. 19 Ole Miss' side of the Student-Athlete Availability Report got cleaned up in Thursday night's update. Quarterback Trinidad Chambliss and wide receiver Deuce Alexander were removed from the report. Both were listed as probable in the initial report Wednesday. Frazier's addition is particularly concerning considering the Rebels are already without star running back Kewan Lacy, who has missed the last two games with a shoulder injury. Without Lacy, Frazier and Shekai Mills-Knight have been responsible for much of the workload in the Rebels' backfield. Starting right guard Patrick Kutas and linebacker Keaton Thomas are among the 11 Rebels ruled out for Saturday's game. Franklin and Denson, meanwhile, remain uncertain after appearing on both availability reports this week. The next update is scheduled for Friday night, with final designations coming before Saturday's kickoff in Norman.
