away.headline: Oklahoma vs. Ole Miss injury report: Who's out and who has to step up for the Sooners
away.blurb: We haven't seen offensive lineman Ryan Fodje out there since the Sooners lost to Kentucky four weeks ago. There's apparently progress, though, as he's at least listed as doubtful after being ruled out early every other week. Sullivan could be more valuable than ever in this game as relief if the Rebels get their running game going and draw out drives to leave OU's defense out there longer. Kenny Ozowalu also spent all of last week on the availability report before playing only two snaps against Florida. His status is actually worse this week, as he's listed as questionable after being probable a week ago. This article was originally published on stormininnorman.com as Oklahoma vs. Ole Miss injury report: Who's out and who has to step up for the Sooners . This is the best injury report for Oklahoma fans to read this season. For only the second time since availability reports were released in 2024, the Sooners actually have fewer players listed than their opponent. Ole Miss is even more ravaged by injury ahead of Sunday's rescheduled matchup in Norman. Most notably, the Rebels will be without star running back Kewan Lacy and starting right guard Patrick Kutas. That still doesn't mean the Sooners are fully healthy, though. There are a few player statuses to keep an eye on before kickoff at noon, and this injury report will be updated until then. Fodje is the last Infinity Stone that Bill Bedenbaugh needs to have a fully healthy starting offensive line this season. Replacement: Where Fodje actually plays when everyone is healthy is still a mystery, but last week, the Sooners' O-line went: Michael Fasusi (LT), Noah Best (LG), Jake Maikkula (C), Heath Ozaeta (RG), E’Marion Harris (RT). Once he's back, Fodje will replace either Ozaeta or Harris. Running back Tory Blaylock had seen an uptick in carries in the last four games and even competed to lead the backfield since he was finally healthy again. Now, he's banged up again. Blaylock has rushed for 178 yards on 42 attempts in eight games this season. He had a season-high 12 carries for 71 yards against Mississippi State. He's still RB2 behind Lloyd Avant, but he should get more touches than usual in a game that interim offensive coordinator Jason Witten will have to rely on the ground attack in while rain pours down. Replacement: Without Blaylock, freshman Jonathan Hatton Jr. should get more touches and maybe his most opportunities of the season if the Sooners keep the ball on the ground. Could we also have an Xavier Robinson sighting? A healthy Cole Sullivan has felt rare this season, as he's played in only five games since transferring from Michigan. He has nine tackles and 0.5 tackles for loss. James Nesta is another depth piece at linebacker, but he sees fewer snaps if Sullivan is healthy. He's recorded 20 tackles this season and recovered a fumble. Ozowalu's versatility makes him a solid depth piece along the defensive line, as he's able to play the interior and on the edge. That could come in hand

away.headline: Injury Report: Ole Miss missing two offensive players against Oklahoma
away.blurb: "And we've been rotating some guys anyway, but he's the only one right now that we know for sure won't be available on Saturday." Injury Report: Ole Miss missing two offensive players against Oklahoma - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF Injury Report: Ole Miss missing two offensive players against Oklahoma Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads The Oklahoma Sooners look to have caught a break ahead of their game with the Ole Miss Rebels on Nov. 14. Ole Miss coach Pete Golding confirmed his squad will be without two of its most important offensive players when the Rebels line up against the Sooners. Golding said running back Kewan Lacy and starting offensive lineman Patrick Kutas will miss the game. So far this season, the Sooners have typically had the least desirable injury report. But the two losses for Ole Miss are fairly significant, especially given the Rebels are coming off their third loss of the season. Golding said Kutas was injured in Ole Miss' 42-7 loss at Georgia on Nov. 7. The Rebels will have to make adjustments across the offensive line. Former Sooner Troy Everett will likely replace Kutas at right guard as he did against Georgia. "Not season-ending," Golding said of Kutas' injury in his weekly presser. "Kutas got banged up pretty good, so we will not have Patrick this week. So there will be some moving parts to that and looking at some guys bumping inside. Golding later clarified Lacy will not play either. Against the Sooners last season, Lacy rushed 27 times for 78 yards and two touchdowns to help No. 8 Ole Miss defeat No. 13 Oklahoma 34–26. This season, however, he has missed a handful of games due to injury. Lacy missed the Georgia game, and it was a noticeable absence. Ole Miss (6-3, 4-3 SEC) mustered only 7 points against the Bulldogs. Lacy was a Doak Walker Award finalist last season. The honor is presented annually to the nation's top college football running back. He has run for five touchdowns this season but hasn't seen the field since dislocating his shoulder against Texas in October. Ole Miss has lost two of the last three games in his absence. Oklahoma (5-4, 3-3 SEC) will have an opportunity to take advantage in Norman with kickoff scheduled for 3:15 p.m. CT. The game will be televised on the SEC Network. This is the third straight season the Sooners have played the Rebels and second straight season Oklahoma has hosted them. The league named the two schools annual rivals last season, meaning they'll play each other at home every season for at least the next four years. Ole Miss is 3-0 against the Sooners, who are trying to build on a 23-7 win over Florida . A win would also keep Oklahoma's bowl streak alive. Injury Report: Ole Miss missing two offensive players against Oklahoma - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF Injury Report: Ole Miss missing two offensive players against Oklahoma Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads The Oklahoma Sooners look to have caught a break ahead of their game with the Ole Miss Rebels on Nov. 14. Ole Miss coach Pete Golding confirmed his squad will be without two of its most important offensive players when the Rebels line up against the Sooners. Golding said running back Kewan Lacy and starting offensive lineman Patrick Kutas will miss the game. So far this season, the Sooners have typically had the least desirable injury report. But the two losses for Ole Miss are fairly significant, especially given the Rebels are coming off their third loss of the season. Golding said Kutas was injured in Ole Miss' 42-7 loss at Georgia on Nov. 7. The Rebels will have to make adjustments across the offensive line. Former Sooner Troy Everett will likely replace Kutas at right guard as he did against Georgia. "Not season-ending," Golding said of Kutas' injury in his weekly presser. "Kutas got banged up pretty good, so we will not have Patrick this week. So there will be some moving parts to that and looking at some guys bumping inside. Golding later clarified Lacy will not play either. Against the Sooners last season, Lacy rushed 27 times for 78 yards and two touchdowns to help No. 8 Ole Miss defeat No. 13 Oklahoma 34–26. This season, however, he has missed a handful of games due to injury. Lacy missed the Georgia game, and it was a noticeable absence. Ole Miss (6-3, 4-3 SEC) mustered only 7 points against the Bulldogs. Lacy was a Doak Walker Award finalist last season. The honor is presented annually to the nation's top college football running back. He has run for five touchdowns this season but hasn't seen the field since dislocating his shoulder against Texas in October. Ole Miss has lost two of the last three games in his absence. Oklahoma (5-4, 3-3 SEC) will have an opportunity to take advantage in Norman with kickoff scheduled for 3:15 p.m. CT. The game will be televised on the SEC Network. This is the third straight season the Sooners have played the Rebels and second straight season Oklahoma has hosted them. The league named the two schools annual rivals last season, meaning they'll play each other at home every season for at least the next four years. Ole Miss is 3-0 against the Sooners, who are trying to build on a 23-7 win over Florida . A win would also keep Oklahoma's bowl streak alive. home.blurb: As the Sooners prepare for the Ole Miss Rebels this Saturday in Norman, Oklahoma, they will have Peyton Bowen available. Bowen was a game-time decision last weekend. Offensive lineman Eddy Pierre-Louis was also a game-time decision against Florida but didn't play. He's probable on the initial availability report and looks like he'll be available for this week. Pierre-Louis hasn't played since the Georgia game. It'll be interesting to see where Pierre-Louis factors into the offensive line rotation with Noah Best and Heath Ozaeta becoming mainstays at guard. Also trending toward making a return this week is defensive back Jacobe Johnson. Johnson has also been out since the Sooners' loss to Georgia but is probable for this week's game against Ole Miss. Cole Sullivan has been in and out of the lineup all season, missing the New Mexico and Georgia games in the first month and missing South Carolina and Florida in recent weeks. His presence at linebacker provides the Sooners with experienced depth behind linebackers Owen Heinecke and Kip Lewis. Sullivan can also bump over and play cheetah to spell Reggie Powers III. Though he's been trending toward a return at some point this season, offensive lineman Ryan Fodje is unlikely to play, coming in as doubtful on the initial availability report. Fodje has been one of the unsung heroes of the offensive line, showing a willingness to play guard, tackle, and center since the Sooners opened fall camp in August. He started at left tackle for Oklahoma from Week 2 until injuring his ankle in the loss to Kentucky. Ole Miss has already ruled out key starters in running back Kewan Lacy and guard Patrick Kutas . picks.blurb: Kentucky vs Florida: Final thoughts, prediction - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football College Football Playoff NFL Power Rankings Week 11 Waiver Wire Chargers get first win College football Top 25 Latest NFL updates Story by Wildcats Wire Kentucky vs Florida: Final thoughts, prediction Braxton Howard, UK Wildcats Wire · Wildcats Wire Fri, November 13, 2026 at 9:57 PM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Will Stein's Kentucky football team hosts Jon Sumrall's Florida Gators team under the lights at Kroger Field tomorrow at 6:15 P.M. ET. Florida has came back down to earth after a strong September and Kentucky is looking to bounce back after suffering their second loss of the season. We preview the Gators offense and defense, as well as laid out the path to victory for the Wildcats. Now, I will give my final thoughts on the matchup and a prediction for the game. Coach Stein said that last week was only the second time in his coaching career that his offense failed to score a touchdown. This team and the offense specifically will be looking to make a statement tomorrow night. They will get a perfect opportunity against a Brad White defense that has struggled all season for the Gators. As we know from watching years of Brad White's scheme in Lexington, they love to play soft zone coverage and allow easy completions to offenses in hopes of executing a bend-don't-break style of defense. The big advantage is this Kentucky offense is built off of efficiency and getting Kenny Minchey easy completions in quick game. This creates an advantageous scheme matchup for Will Stein and offensive coordinator Joe Sloan. If the Wildcats can eliminate the self-inflicted mistakes from last week in Knoxville, you have to like their chances to put together long scoring drives. The difference in this game being close and the Cats running away with it is if the offense can start to find the explosive plays. One area of this matchup we have not talked about is the weather aspect of this football game on Saturday. The past few days in Lexington have turned extremely cold, and temperatures for kickoff at looking at 40 degrees or below. Combine that with the winds, it will be freezing at Kroger Field and will only get colder as the game goes on. You have to wonder how this Florida team will respond in these conditions especially if they don't start fast in this one. This Florida team is reeling, they have lost four of their last five games. The drop-off has been eye-opening for the Gators because they looked like one of the best teams in the country through the first month of the season. Defenses have figured out how to bottle up their run game and the offense has started to suffer because of it. The Gators offense led them to their hot start to the Jon Sumrall era and covered up the rough play on the defensive side of the football. Kentucky has to stop this rushing attack and get Florida into a dropback heavy game. The Gators are going back to Aaron Philo after starting Tramell Jones last week. The old saying goes: if you have two quarterbacks, you have none. I think the Wildcats will be prepared to potentially see both guys this week as the Gators will try everything they can to generate some offense. Florida has to answer questions offensively, their offensive line is one of the worst in the conference and the quarterback situation is not ideal. Brad White has not figured out how to fix the Gators defensive issues in his first year away from Lexington. I think Kentucky capitalizes on that and has one of their best offensive performances of the season following last week where they failed to reach the end zone. Kentucky has their backs against the wall, they will make the College Football Playoff if they win the last three games and I believe the offense makes a statement in the cold at Kroger Field. Prediction: Kentucky 38, Florida 20 This article originally appeared on UK Wildcats Wire: Kentucky vs Florida: Final thoughts, prediction

Mandatory Credit: Randy Sartin-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters) Stephan Stroud · SEC Country Thu, November 12, 2026 at 9:03 PM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Florida Gators are heading to Lexington looking to turn their season around when they take on the Kentucky Wildcats in a major SEC matchup on Saturday, November 14. Both teams are coming off disappointing losses, but the stakes are much higher for Kentucky, which is still fighting to keep its College Football Playoff hopes alive. Kentucky enters the matchup with a 7-2 overall record and a 5-2 mark in SEC play. Meanwhile, Florida sits at 5-4 and 3-4 in conference play. With the Wildcats playing in front of their home crowd at Kroger Field, they will have an opportunity to get back on track against a Florida team desperately searching for consistency. Florida Looking for Offensive Answers Florida has struggled to find consistency offensively over the past several weeks. The Gators started the season 4-0 and looked like a potential threat in the SEC, but they have since lost four of their last five games. Head coach Jon Sumrall will need to find a way to get his offense moving again after Florida scored just seven points in its 23-7 loss to Oklahoma last weekend. One of the biggest storylines entering Saturday's game is Florida's quarterback situation. Aaron Philo is expected to return to the starting position after Tramell Jones Jr. started against Oklahoma. Philo has thrown for 1,367 yards and nine touchdowns this season while completing 70.5% of his passes. However, Philo will need to take better care of the football and avoid costly mistakes against a Kentucky defense looking to create opportunities. The Gators will also need a big performance from running back Jadan Baugh. He has been one of Florida's most important offensive players this season, rushing for 836 yards and 14 touchdowns. Establishing the running game could take pressure off Philo and help Florida control the pace of the matchup. Kentucky Looking to Bounce Back Kentucky enters Saturday's contest with plenty to prove after suffering a disappointing 34-6 loss to Tennessee last weekend. The Wildcats had won six consecutive games before that defeat and will be looking to show that one bad performance does not define their season. Head coach Will Stein has put together an impressive first season in Lexington, leading Kentucky to a 7-2 record. However, the Wildcats cannot afford another disappointing performance if they want to remain in the College Football Playoff conversation. Quarterback Kenny Minchey will be one of the most important players to watch. Minchey has thrown for 1,979 yards and 14 touchdowns while recording just two interceptions. His ability to protect the football and make plays through the air has been a major part of Kentucky's success. The Wildcats will also look to get their rushing attack back on track after struggling against Tennessee. Running back C.J. Baxter has rushed for 541 yards and eight touchdowns this season, giving Kentucky another important offensive weapon. A Must Win Opportunity for Both Teams Saturday's matchup presents an important opportunity for both programs. Florida needs a statement victory to get its season moving in the right direction, while Kentucky needs to respond to last week's loss and protect its playoff hopes. The quarterback matchup between Philo and Minchey could ultimately make the difference. Florida has the offensive talent to challenge Kentucky, but the Wildcats have been more consistent throughout the season. With home-field advantage and more to lose in the playoff race, Kentucky will have plenty of motivation. However, Florida has an opportunity to make a statement and potentially deliver one of the biggest results of its season. The Gators have one more big challenge ahead in the regular season, and it's not one anyone saw coming before the year began. The Gators head to Kentucky, who remains on the cusp of a stunning SEC championship game appearance. The Wildcats (7-2, 5-2) are off to their best start since 2018 under first-year coach Will Stein. Their chances of sneaking into the College Football Playoff took a big hit when their six-game winning streak ended with a 34-6 loss last week at Tennessee. Florida has fallen to 5-4 (3-4) in its first season under Jon Sumrall amid a 1-4 slide since October began. One big thing that's helped is their ability to force turnovers: The Wildcats have 18 takeaways this year, tied for sixth-most in the nation, and their four picks against John Mateer helped them win a weird game at Oklahoma four weeks ago. Tramell Jones has thrown five INTs this year, including three over the Gators' current two-game losing streak. UF's turnover margin of -3 slots them in the bottom third of FBS. If Jadan Baugh and the run game can recover its mojo from earlier in the year, the Gators could do what Tennessee did to the Wildcats last week (240 yards, three TDs on the ground), but until it shows signs of life, it's too much to expect that. With CJ Baxter leading the way, Kentucky has the SEC's sixth-ranked run game, one spot behind Florida. Theirs has been more sustained over the course of the season; even in last week's blowout loss, UK still ran for 3.7 yards per carry against the Vols, as opposed to UF's 2.8 ypc vs. Oklahoma. UF ranks 12th in the SEC in giving up 134.7 rushing yards per game, not a great stat especially when hitting the road. The Utes are ranked No. 2 in the latest CFP poll as one of two undefeated teams remaining. After beating their hated rivals BYU last week, Utah's path to the Playoff -- and the Big 12 title game -- is clear, but they must turn the page quickly from taking down the Cougars as a trip to Tucson could prove tricky. Arizona climbed to No. 23 in this week's rankings after beating TCU in a thriller, and the 7-2 Wildcats' only losses this season have been to the other top teams in the Big 12 -- BYU and Texas Tech . Both of those losses came on the road, and Arizona will be relishing the opportunity to prove they belong in the top tier of the Big 12 when they finally get to welcome one of the big boys to southern Arizona. For the Utes, a win writes their name into the CFP bracket in pencil, as they'd improve to 10-0 with two games left where they'd be heavy favorites over TCU and West Virginia . The Wildcats, meanwhile, can pick up the biggest win of Brent Brennan's tenure and solidify their place in the Big 12's upper tier. The game was originally scheduled for the 7:30 p.m. ET primetime slot on Saturday, but due to travel issues caused by the FAA shutdown on Friday , kickoff was moved to 10:30 p.m. for this pivotal showdown. Where to watch Utah vs. Arizona live Date : Saturday, Nov. 14 | Time : 10:30 p.m. ET Location : Casino Del Sol Stadium -- Tucson, Arizona TV: Fox | Live stream: Fubo (try free) Utah vs. Arizona: Need to know Refocusing the Utes: The Utes put everything they had into winning The Holy War last week against BYU, in the first-ever matchup between the rivals while both were ranked in the top 10. It was obvious how much they put into the game plan with their hot start, and then they were forced to dig deep and rally after the Cougars answered with some haymakers of their own. That win was a proof point for Morgan Scalley in his first season as head coach, but this week might show us more about the kind of culture he's building in Salt Lake City. There's a natural urge to exhale after that kind of win, but Arizona is going to be juiced up for the chance to face the No. 2 team in the country at home. The Utes have to find a way to match that energy -- or at least withstand an early onslaught -- and get the game back on their terms. Strength on strength in the pass game: Arizona is one of the best passing offenses in the country with veteran quarterback Noah Fifita who is both efficient with a 73% completion rate and dynamic with 23 pass plays of 30-plus yards -- third-most in the country. Fifita and his favorite target Isaiah Mizell can take the lid off of most defenses and apply constant stress -- especially with Fifita's ability to extend plays and get outside the pocket. However, they'll be going up against one of the nation's best pass defenses that had Bear Bachmeier completely lost a week ago. Utah is allowing opposing quarterbacks to complete just 51.3% of passes (2nd lowest in the country) and is tied for fourth in interceptions with 13 (including four last week). The Utes pass defense is hyper aggressive, and they have four players with two or more interceptions this season. If there is one weakness to the Utah defense, it is that they have been susceptible to big plays in the passing game. The Utes have allowed 15 pass plays of 30+ yards this season, which ranks 104th in the country. Fifita and Arizona will have to take advantage of those opportunities for chunk plays when they present themselves because moving the ball consistently against the Utes is incredibly difficult. Arizona's pass rush vs. Devon Dampier : The Utes defense will get plenty of attention, but Arizona hasn't been a slouch on that side of the ball this year either. The strength of their defense is their pass rush, which is 10th in the nation in sacks per game (3.11). Devon Dampier is a tough quarterback to wrangle with his combination of strength and elusiveness, but the Wildcats are going to try to heat up Dampier to create some negative plays or, more ideally, turnovers. How Utah's offensive line handles Arizona's rush and how Dampier manages plays when the Wildcats do get pressure on him will be critical in this game. Utah has allowed just 13 sacks this season, thanks to a quality offensive line and Dampier's escapability, but that will be put to the test against the Wildcats. If Arizona is going to win this game, they need to find ways to get the Utes' offense behind the sticks and probably need to win the turnover battle. The pass rush is going to be their best weapon to accomplish both of those goals, and if Arizona is going to pull off the upset, expect the pass rush to be leading the charge. Utah vs. Arizona prediction, picks The Wildcats are a good football team and should provide a big test for the Utes coming off last week's win. That said, so far this season, when Arizona has played the best teams in the Big 12, it has proven to be lagging just a bit behind. Over 60 minutes, I expect that to be the case again on Saturday, even with a raucous environment in Tucson for their biggest home game in years. Utah won't have it easy, but when the clock hits triple zeroes, I expect the Utes to move to 10-0 and cover the short number. Josh Furlong: "The easy answer is quarterback Devon Dampier, who has been healthy and efficient as the team's biggest playmaker, but it ultimately comes down to the culture Morgan Scalley has built at Utah in such a short time. He's allowing the players to be loose while focused, understanding that it takes each person to contribute to wins. He's an extremely competitive coach, but he's able to pair that with a system that allows players to make mistakes, grow and develop." Arizona fans still have nightmares about Devon Dampier from two years ago at New Mexico, and he seems to have only gotten better. Where has his game most improved this season, and is there anything he still struggles with? "Dampier has worked on going through his progressions and staying in the pocket more, which has allowed Utah to do more with him at QB. It's giving him more structure while understanding that he still needs room to freelance and be the dynamic QB he can be. All of that has allowed him to have more confidence, especially now that he's been paired with a better group of wide receivers. At times, though, he gets happy feet and doesn't have the right mechanics in his throws, which can sometimes limit his passing." Wayshawn Parker apparently got banged up against BYU but should be good to go for this game. What does he bring to the offense when healthy? "Wayshawn Parker simply opens up the options for Utah's offense. His threat as a runner, especially as he breaks through tackles, makes him one of the top offensive names you have to take away. But by doing so, opposing defenses have to handle many other players that can be just as effective in advancing the offense — Dampier, Daniel Bray, Byrd Ficklin, Braden Pegan, Creed Whittemore, etc. On top of that, he's really developed a great pass blocking game, which has been a huge advantage in keeping Dampier upright and doing what he does." Arizona's secondary has been dealing with injuries and got exploited a bit last week with deep passes. Who would be the beneficiaries of this in the Ute receiving corps? "The primary receiving target would be Braden Pegan (WR1), who is a multi-faceted receiver who can do pretty much anything needed, and is paired with Ricky Johnson and Creed Whittemore. Johnson is a smooth runner with great separation and great hands. Whittemore works primarily in the slot and has been great in the intermediate game, especially with opposing defenses focusing on Pegan and the potential run threats of Dampier, Ficklin, Parker. Another option is tight end Noah Bennee, who is the benefactor of all the other skills players being the top of mind. As the defense focuses on other players, Bennee sneaks out and can be a problem with his size." How do you expect Utah to defend Arizona's passing attack? "Utah will primarily operate in man coverage and force Noah Fifita to beat them one-on-one, while the defensive coordinator Colton Swan schemes up disguises and blitzes to keep Fifita uncomfortable. Because Fifita is so explosive, it's likely Utah will try more contain while pressuring him." Morgan Scalley had been the coach in waiting at Utah for a while, and we're seeing why with this 9-0 start. What are the biggest differences between him and Kyle Whittingham? "The biggest difference is that Scalley is a people's person. Kyle Whittingham cared more about coaching football and not the other elements, whereas Scalley sees it all interconnected. He shares the same hard-nosed, physical approach of Whittingham but wants a connected team that has no factions. It's not, offense gets to know offense and defense gets to know defense, it's a team-wide look as each works to understand the other. He's also open to feedback, assuming that the feedback actually is presented in a way that helps change and it's just complaining, though he'd listen to anyone who is frustrated. He wants all to feel connected and bought into the program, regardless of their standing with the team." Prediction time. Does Utah move one step closer to an unbeaten regular season or does Arizona pull off a November upset at home and stay in the hunt for the Big 12 title game and the playoffs? Give us a score pick. "This game in Tucson is always a tricky one. Even when Utah has been the clear favorite, it's far from a decisive win for the Utes. I think Scalley has his squad more focused on this game than it might have been in year's past, which leads me to believe Utah will be ready for any blow and not be caught off guard in a road environment. I think Utah is the more complete team, but they've got to stop Fifita. To me, Utah wins this game if they can contain Fifita (as much as possible) and cannot give up momentum to an opposing crowd. I see Utah winning something like 31-24 ."

picks.blurb: Arizona Wildcats football vs. Utah Utes score predictions | Arizona Desert Swarm Skip to main content SB Nation SB Nation logo An Arizona Wildcats Community Arizona Desert Swarm November 17, 2026 Arizona Desert Swarm Notifications Notifications The Feed Sections Arizona Basketball Arizona Football Arizona Softball Arizona Recruiting Arizona Soccer Arizona Volleyball Arizona Baseball Arizona Gymnastics Arizona in the Pros Betting Betting News FanDuel College Football Odds FanDuel College Basketball Odds Arizona Football Odds Arizona Basketball Odds College Football Picks and Predictions College Basketball Picks and Predictions Login / Sign Up Search The Feed Sections Expand Arizona Basketball Betting Expand Betting News Community Guidelines All communities Notifications Arizona Football Twice this season, Arizona has found itself up against a ranked opponent with a chance to make a big splash on the national stage, and both times it led at halftime only to fall in the end. Third time’s a charm? No. 22 Arizona (7-2, 4-2) plays its biggest game of the year on Saturday, hosting unbeaten No. 2 Utah (9-0, 6-0) with a chance to climb back into the Big 12 title race and the hunt for a College Football Playoff spot. How will the Wildcats do in this Top 25 clash? Our staff makes its predictions. Kim Doss — Utah wins 30-28 Utah is not a team that has difficulty scoring. The Utes average 34.3 points per game against their FBS opponents this season. Their lowest output was 21 points against Houston. They’ve only been held below 30 points by three of their FBS opponents: Houston, BYU, and (surprisingly) Colorado. Arizona will be Utah’s third ranked opponent but first on the road. Will it matter that the game isn’t in Salt Lake City? Doubtful. The Wildcats had issues with mobile quarterbacks. While Arizona is ranked fifth in the Big 12 with 203.3 pashing yards allowed per game, Devon Dampier doesn’t just rely on his arm to move the ball. He throws for 228.1 ypg. He’s also second on the team in rushing with 53.6 ypg on the ground. Dampier is going to be playing in his home state against his former head coach. The now-assistant coach at Arizona admits that he should have played Dampier more when they were both at New Mexico. The senior from Phoenix may have something to prove and a group of friends and family members in attendance to prove it to. On the positive side, Arizona should be able to move the ball, too. Utah is ninth in the Big 12 in passing yards allowed at 233.8 per game. Noah Fifita is fourth in the nation in passing yards per game (310.4), total passing yards (2,794), and total offense per game (325.4). The Arizona defense has been solid for most of the year, but it barely kept the Big 12’s 15 th -ranked scoring offense under 30 points last week. Utah is the No. 2 scoring offense in the league. The Wildcats are No. 6. To make matters worse for the ‘Cats, Utah has the No. 2 scoring defense in the Big 12. Arizona’s in No. 5. With some luck, this one could be close. It would be a shocker to see Arizona pull off the upset, though. Ezra Amacher — Utah wins 27-24 Utah’s Devon Dampier is the type of quarterback that gives Arizona defensive coordinator Danny Gonzales cold sweats at night. The senior from Saguaro High School in Phoenix has grown into one of top dual-threat quarterbacks in the country. He ranks second among all active FBS quarterbacks with 2,811 career rushing yards. He has a dang good arm as well and doesn’t commit many turnovers. Arizona struggled to stop the other dual-threat QBs it faced this year in TCU’s Jaden Craig and West Virginia’s Michael Hawkins Jr. Dampier is better than either of them and has a stalwart offensive line protecting him. I don’t see the Wildcats defense being able to do enough to keep Utah off the board. That wouldn’t be as much of a concern against a lesser opponent, but Utah’s defense is outstanding. The Utes give up 16.3 points per game, second-fewest in the Big 12. They’re riding high on confidence after forcing BYU’s Bear Bachmeier into four interceptions last week. I give Utah the edge. Adam Green — Arizona wins 31 -27 Why the hell not. Here in this space is where I try to convince you all (and myself, really) that this pick is an actual prediction rather than wischasting. So here we go. Arizona is good — very good — at home. Utah has not beaten a ranked team on the road. Arizona has everything to play for and is coming off a victory that likely served as a wake up call while inspiring confidence. Utah, on the other hand, has a little bit of breathing room and is coming off an emotional and physical victory over rival BYU. Finally, Arizona has Noah Fifita . The QB is a perfect 2-0 against Morgan Scalley’s defense, with the most recent victory coming in Salt Lake City during a season in which the Wildcats were not a particularly good team. That Fifita is playing the best football of his career heading into this game and has weapons like Isaiah Mizell and Giovanni Richardson is nothing to feel bad about. This isn’t to say that it will be an easy game like the last time these teams played in Tucson, because it’s hard to imagine No. 2 in the nation going down without a fight. Utah’s offense is going to be more dynamic than we’re used to seeing but their defense is gettable for an Arizona team that is quite capable of slinging the ball around. Keep penalties to a minimum and win the turnover battle, and Arizona will win the game. Juan Serrano — Arizona wins 31-28 Arizona is a different team when it plays inside Casino Del Sol Stadium. Of course, last week’s game was a miracle and not usually how the Wildcats play at home. The defense did only surrendered 21 points to TCU which is usually a winning formula. Noah Fifita ’s pick-six was a rarity and kept the Horned Frogs in the game. He cannot afford to have those type of plays against Utah, and I don’t think he will. Fifita usually has some of his best games against the Utes. I also think Arizona missed two shots at a big win against BYU and Texas Tech. It’s time for the ball to bounce in the way of the Wildcats in terms of making a statement. Utah has only been favored by 2.5 since the end of the Holy War, and it has stuck there. That is a very good sign for Arizona. Devon Dampier does present a big issue for the defense but I would not be surprised if Danny Gonzales presents a different picture for Dampier. He knows his defense has struggled against mobile quarterbacks and it has shown in many games. Something will need to change schematically for the Wildcats to have a chance to win. It all comes down to what is at stake for Arizona. This is a season defining, program defining moment for Brent Brennan ’s squad. The home winning streak will continue for the Wildcats and will earn one of the most historic wins in Arizona football history. Brandon Combs — Arizona wins 30-24 I’m not going to lie, I’ve been tossing this one back and forth in my mind. The Wildcats at home are a force to be reckoned with. I throw out the issues from Arizona last week as kind of fluky. They were coming off an emotional loss against Texas Tech, and on a short week no less. Noah Fifita’s rare and odd pick six, Dwight Bootle’s rough night and the not-great tackling were all things that caused the closeness of the game against TCU. On the other side, you have Utah coming off an physical and emotional Holy War win against BYU last week. As of this writing, Utah looks like they’ll be without their leader in sacks, DL Karson Kaufusi , who has 3 sacks this year. However, the Utes still have Jireh Moe and Elijah Elliss , who are also fantastic d-linemen and have combined for 62 tackles, 9.5 TFLs and 5 sacks. Overall, this game is going to come down to QB play. Not breaking any news here, but Noah is a stud and will have to play a near flawless game. If he plays his game and doesn’t force anything, or make any plays like last week’s pick six, Arizona has a legit chance to win. For the Utes, Devon Dampier is a problem. He has been effective through the air this season, however, his legs are his biggest strength. He is a fantastic runner and is Utah’s second leading rusher. Even if he doesn’t gain massive yards, he is able to extend plays and forces the defense to respect his running ability. Finally, I think Danny Gonzales will change some things up for Utah. I don’t expect to see the same looks that TCU got, mainly due to the injuries on defense. I believe Danny has learned from the Tommy Castellanos issues and won’t make it as easy for Dampier. Couple that with slowing down Wayshawn Parker and playing in front of what seems to be turning into a packed Sol, I think the defense can do it. Brian Pedersen — Arizona wins 21-20 As I wrote earlier this week , November has traditionally been the month when Arizona has picked up its biggest home wins. It’s been a while, though, and most of those have been when the Wildcats are a decided underdog and the game isn’t in the national spotlight. Not the case this time, with a very small spread and Fox’s Big Noon Kickoff is in town. The losses at BYU and Texas Tech had a common theme beyond leading at halftime. Both saw the UA struggle mightily in the second half, scoring only nine total points, though each time it was down four and driving with a chance to go back in front. One missed play turned everything. Utah is a very good team with no weakness, and has the kind of dual-threat weapon in Devon Dampier that Arizona traditionally struggles with. But it’s November, and strange things happen at night in the desert. Arizona linebacker Chase Kennedy gestures to the crowd behind the end zone after registering a sack in the second quarter of the game against Northern Arizona on Sept. 5. 7 Chase Kennedy vs. 15 Byrd Ficklin With Arizona's defensive secondary in question due to a number of injuries — like cornerback Jay'Vion Cole, safeties Cam Chapa and Quinn Olson and slot cornerback Malcolm Hartzog — Saturday will be a test for Arizona's front six, including Kennedy, who played two seasons at Utah in 2022 and '23. Kennedy has 15 stops at the line of scrimmage this season, per PFF. Rather than following head coach Kyle Whittingham to Michigan or entering the transfer portal, the second-year Ficklin stayed at Utah and has been the other component of Utah's two-quarterback system, albeit Devon Dampier is the starting quarterback and primary passer. The left-handed Ficklin's athleticism and dual-threat abilities give Utah a wrinkle on offense. Arizona head coach Brent Brennan shouts encouragement to the offense trying to get in the end zone in third quarter against TCU during their Big 12 game, Tucson, Ariz., Nov. 6, 2026. When Utah has the ball … Utah's offensive coordinator Kevin McGiven and quarterbacks coach Ryan Gunderson worked for Arizona head coach Brent Brennan at San Jose State. Brennan's former assistants have put together one of the most creative and effective offenses in the Big 12, a unit that uses two defensive tackles — 317-pound Semi Taulanga and Sione Motuapuaka — as tight ends and fullbacks. When Arizona has the ball … Arizona quarterback Noah Fifita has developed a highly effective connection with the receiver tandem of Isaiah Mizell and Giovanni Richardson, a sophomore tandem that has a combined 77 catches, 1,201 yards and seven touchdowns this season — Mizell with all of the touchdowns. Taking care of the ball is imperative for Fifita against a defense that is tops in the Big 12 in interceptions. College Football 27 prediction: UA 26, Utah 21 Arizona took a 23-14 lead in the early moments of the fourth quarter following a 51-yard field goal by kicker Michael Salgado-Medina, who made two field goals earlier in the game. Salgado-Medina made his fourth field goal on Arizona's second-to-last drive of the game and the Wildcats led 26-14. Arizona wide receiver Isaiah Mizell had six catches for 100 yards and two touchdowns, including a 56-yard score on a slant route on fourth-and-2 on Arizona's opening drive. Despite Utah getting within a possession, Arizona picked up three first downs on its final drive and forced Utah to burn all of its timeouts. After Arizona punter Chase Ridley pinned the Utes on the 1-yard line, Utah had 30 seconds to go to the length of the field. Utah ran out of time. Wildcats win. Now the Longhorns get back out on the road, and this time it's to one of the toughest places to play, not just in the SEC but in the country, traveling to Baton Rouge to take on the LSU Tigers this weekend. The Texas Longhorns on SI make their prediction for Saturday night's battle in Death Valley. Texas Longhorns defensive back Bo Mascoe (5) reacts after an interception towards the end of the game against the Missouri Tigers at Faurot Field at Memorial Stadium. | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Leo Barnes Yes, Saturday’s matchup against LSU will be at night, and yes, it will be in Death Valley. But the Longhorns have won three straight, and perhaps more importantly, Arch Manning is playing some of his best football with a level of confidence that was noticeably absent earlier in the season. Of course, I’m not going to overlook the Texas offensive line’s issues — even if it did show improvement last week against Missouri — or an LSU defensive front that’s been relentless all season. But I also don’t see Sam Leavitt having an easy night against Will Muschamp’s defense. I expect a physical, relatively low-scoring affair, with both defenses controlling stretches of the game. But I like Texas just enough to escape Baton Rouge relatively unscathed with its fourth consecutive victory. Texas 27, LSU 20 This game comes down to how often the LSU pass rush can get home. If they can make Manning uncomfortable and force him into mistakes, the Tigers can move the ball on the Longhorns, but red zone stops will be the difference. picks.headline: Three Bold Predictions for Texas' Saturday Night Showdown Against LSU
picks.blurb: Three Bold Predictions for Texas' Saturday Night Showdown Against LSU Skip to main content SI.COM LONGHORNS NEWS 2025 Football Bracket FOOTBALL FOOTBALL FOOTBALL NEWS 2023 FOOTBALL COMMITS SI.COM LONGHORNS FB BASKETBALL NEWS SI.COM LONGHORNS BB The trouble with bold predictions is they tend to sound a little ridiculous — right up until they happen. There are plenty of reasonable expectations for Saturday night’s matchup between Texas and LSU. But reasonable expectations aren’t all that interesting, are they? So let’s throw a little caution to the wind. Maybe these predictions will look brilliant by the final whistle. Maybe they’ll be aging poorly before halftime. But that’s half the fun in the first place. Here are three bold predictions for the Longhorns’ trip to Baton Rouge. Raleek Brown Rushes for Over 100 Yards Nov 7, 2026; Columbia, Missouri, USA; Texas Longhorns running back Raleek Brown runs the ball during the first half against the Missouri Tigers at Faurot Field at Memorial Stadium. William Purnell-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect On paper, this might be the boldest prediction of the three. On paper, this might be the boldest prediction of the three. LSU enters Saturday allowing just 84.7 rushing yards per game, the second-best mark in the SEC. Meanwhile Texas has struggled to establish consistency on the ground for much of the season. But if there’s a Longhorn capable of bucking that trend, it’s Raleek Brown. Against Ole Miss, Brown demonstrated what an elite Texas run game could look like given the opportunity, carrying the ball 23 times for 157 yards. Last weekend, he once again flashed that potential, rushing for 85 yards on 17 attempts. With Sarkisian emphasizing the importance of avoiding situations where Texas falls behind the chains, establishing the run game early will likely be a priority. That could mean a concerted effort to feed Brown from the opening drive, allowing him to find his rhythm. It certainly won't be easy against an LSU defensive front that has made life miserable for opposing running backs all season. But if Sarkisian can get Brown going, don't be surprised if he eclipses the century mark. Colin Simmons Records Three Sacks Oct 10, 2026; Dallas, Texas, USA; Texas Longhorns defensive end Colin Simmons in action during the game against the Oklahoma Sooners at the Cotton Bowl. Before his ankle injury, it would’ve been fair to argue that Colin Simmons was the best defensive player in the nation. Through his first six games, the junior accumulated 10.5 sacks — a metric he still leads the SEC in despite missing more than 2 games — and 16 tackles for loss. After playing just 18 snaps against Missouri, Simmons has yet to fully establish himself as the disruptive force that terrorized opposing offenses earlier in the season. Saturday might change that. LSU quarterback Sam Leavitt was sacked four times against Alabama last weekend, and Texas’ defensive front will prove to be another difficult assignment. But perhaps the most intriguing aspect of this prediction is Leavitt’s style of play. Leavitt has demonstrated a willingness to escape the pocket and improvise when plays begin to break down, often extending plays with his legs in hopes of creating something out of nothing. And while that ability makes him a dangerous dual-threat quarterback, it could also present an opportunity for a player with Simmons’ speed and relentless pursuit. Simmons doesn't necessarily need to beat his blocker immediately to disrupt a play. His closing speed allows him to pursue quarterbacks well after they've escaped the initial pressure, potentially turning Leavitt's improvisation into opportunities for sacks. Yes, three sacks is asking a lot, especially from a player still working his way back from an ankle injury. But if Simmons is even close to full strength, there's little reason to believe he can't once again take over a game. Texas Forces Three Turnovers Nov 7, 2026; Baton Rouge, Louisiana, USA; LSU Tigers quarterback Sam Leavitt looks to pass the ball during the second half against Alabama Crimson Tide at Tiger Stadium. Stephen Lew-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Nine interceptions in nine games. Nine interceptions in nine games. That’s the rather alarming statistic surrounding Leavitt , even if those numbers don’t necessarily tell the full story. Not all nine interceptions have been his fault. But Leavitt has shown a tendency to misread defenders dropping into coverage and force throws into crowded windows, mistakes that Texas could be well-positioned to exploit. The Tigers have committed 13 turnovers this season, including four lost fumbles. And while Texas has forced just 10 turnovers through nine games, with Simmons healthy, Rasheem Biles playing some of his best football and a secondary capable of capitalizing on hurried throws, the Longhorns have all the pieces to give Texcalibur quite the night. Published Nov 14, 2026 LEO BARNES Leo Barnes is a junior journalism major at the University of Texas at Austin. He is also a senior sports reporter for The Daily Texan, where he currently covers the men’s basketball beat. Born and raised in Austin, Barnes roots for all things Texas, as well as the San Antonio Spurs and Dallas Cowboys. picks.headline: Brian Kelly's Official Prediction for Texas-LSU Matchup Might Surprise You
picks.blurb: Brian Kelly's Official Prediction for Texas-LSU Matchup Might Surprise You Skip to main content SI.COM LONGHORNS NEWS 2025 Football Bracket FOOTBALL FOOTBALL FOOTBALL NEWS 2023 FOOTBALL COMMITS SI.COM LONGHORNS FB BASKETBALL NEWS SI.COM LONGHORNS BB Former LSU Tigers head coach Brian Kelly believes Lane Kiffin's squad will pick up the win in Week 11 when the Texas Longhorns travel to Baton Rouge for a battle under the lights. He made his official prediction with CBS Sports this week. Kelly doesn't believe the Longhorns' offensive line will be up to the task of protecting quarterback Arch Manning against an elite LSU pass rush. "I've always felt that by the 10th week of the season, you are who you are. And I think those things will show with Texas and the inability to protect the quarterback. I worry about that," Kelly said about Texas's protection on CBS Sports airwaves . "For LSU, it's situational offense in particular. They were 0-for-4 on fourth down (against Alabama last week), and they were abysmal in the red zone. But I think you can fix those things, so I'm leaning toward LSU making the adjustments that they need to and winning the football game." Some fans might have expected Kelly to pick Texas for a few reasons. For starters, the Longhorns have a better collection of wins and are on a three-game winning streak. But on top of that, the narrative is that Kelly had some sort of grudge against LSU and will look to pick against them at every turn. However, Kelly's comments make it clear that he's confident in what LSU brings to the table in this matchup. Before the season, Goosby's continuity at left tackle was seen as a bedrock for the group's ability to give Manning time to operate in the pocket. Andre Cojoe has given up almost twice the pressure that Goosby did, necessitating a move to right tackle almost immediately, while Melvin Siani has had struggles on the blindside in Goosby's stead. It's been rough sledding since Goosby went down in the first quarter against the Ole Miss Rebels in Week 8. Blake Baker's defensive schemes have boosted LSU's talent up front this season. The Tigers have one of the best pass rushes in the SEC, with three different players having at least five sacks through the first nine games of the season. LSU defensive end Princewill Umanmielen leads the defense with 8.5 sacks, while Jordan Ross has five sacks, three pass deflections, and a 30-yard pick six as the cherry on top. Meanwhile, in the middle, Deuce Geralds has been a force through the A-gap. Geralds has five sacks and has caught up to speed against the run. UT may not have a tougher test all season than this defensive front. It makes it even harder when you account for Manning and Steve Sarkisian's communication issues against a Tiger Stadium crowd at night. We'll see if Kyle Flood's group has the chops to keep it together for the offensive skill-position players behind them in Death Valley during a major matchup for the CFP's sake. See the latest Texas-LSU lines on Kalshi , where LSU carries a 61% win probability, plus our Week 11 Top Picks and Brad Powers' Week 11 predictions . Who will win Texas vs LSU today: Texas +4.5 It's hard to have much faith in either of these programs, but Texas has been the more consistent team this season and seems to have turned a corner. The Longhorns have covered in three straight games, two against Top 25 teams, and I like them at +2.5 or better against LSU . Since its upset loss to Florida, Texas has outscored opponents 99-50 with Arch Manning playing far more consistently (nine total TDs, two interceptions). LSU hasn't shown up in any of its games against quality opponents, failing to cover in all three of its matchups against currently ranked programs . In those three games, Sam Leavitt threw as many touchdowns as interceptions (3) and was sacked nine times with a 21.1% pressure-to-sack rate. If his Jekyll and Hyde play shows up against a Texas defense ranked No. 5 in success rate (36.6%), LSU will lose. See our college football picks against the spread for more Week 11 sides. TOP PICK Texas vs LSU Over/Under pick today: Under 46.5 Steve Sarkisian and Lane Kiffin are known for their offenses, but both have elite defenses carrying their teams this season. With how sporadic Manning and Leavitt have been, especially in high-profile games, I'd play the Under at 45.5 or better . Manning has been one of the most mistake-prone QBs in the country this season, with the 11th-highest turnover-worthy play rate (4%) and the fifth-highest pressure-to-sack rate in the P4 (27.2%). And LSU's defense is as disruptive as it gets, ranking third nationally in sacks (36) and fourth in havoc rate (22.2%). The Longhorns' defense is nearly as opportunistic, too, ranking 11th nationally in havoc rate (20%), and it's getting the best defensive player in the country back in full force. away.blurb: For No. 8 Texas (8-2, 5-2), the dreams of the playoffs continue while LSU will look to still get the taste of defeat out of its mouth as it hits the road next week to face No. 9 Tennessee at 2:30 p.m. CT on Saturday, Nov. 21 inside Neyland Stadium in Knoxville. Longhorns have the ball but if you're an LSU fan, your defense is the unit you want on the field to try and close this game out. Tigers have limited Texas to just 217 yards of offense and have forced three turnovers. Slowly but surely, Texas is getting back into this game as Gianni Spetic knocks in his third field goal of the game. He knocked this one in from 50 yards out to shrink LSU's lead to just five points. The Tigers have been living and dying in the air for the most part of this game until running back Dillin Jones found a lane. Jones broke out for a 44-yard rushing touchdown to extend LSU's lead. The run marks the longest rush of the night so far as both teams haven't run it a ton with success. That last possession of the half for LSU was a dud. Once the offense got close to the end zone, Texas' defense bowed up and LSU fizzled out. Leavitt just lobbed that ball up. I know the pressure is in his face but he's got to rifle that ball out of the back of the end zone. LSU OC Charlies Weis Jr. had Leavitt roll out plenty to avoid Texas' army of pass rushers. Get used to seeing that a lot tonight. After falling to Alabama last Saturday and suffering its third loss on the 2026 season, LSU couldn’t afford to lose against Texas inside Tiger Stadium on Saturday, Nov. 14. With their backs against the wall Lane Kiffin and his Tigers (6-4, 3-4 SEC) battled for every point while also trying to neutralize Texas’ star quarterback Arch Manning. In the end, Manning pulled off the second half heroics to help the Longhorns storm back and beat LSU 22-21. Thus ending the Tigers dream of making it to the College Football Playoff. It was far from pretty on offense for the Tigers. Quarterback Sam Leavitt matched his season-high in interceptions, throwing three. Interceptions were the theme of the night, with both Leavitt and Manning combining for six picks. Despite it, Manning and company only needed the final two minutes to go right as he finished the night throwing for 174 yards and a 4-yard game-winning touchdown. Defensively, LSU held the Longhorns to a season-low in points as they brought pressure almost every snap, making it hard for Manning to do what he does best; use he’s legs and pick defenses apart.
